The '''2022–23 season''' was [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal Football Club]]'s 31st season in the [[Premier League]], their [[List of Arsenal F.C. seasons|97th consecutive season]] in the [[English football league system|top flight]] of English football and 106th season in the top flight overall.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/features/48523/behind-the-numbers- |title=All-time Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=18 Jun 2013 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=22 Jun 2023 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230622042610/https://www.arsenal.com/news/features/48523/behind-the-numbers- |archive-date=22 Jun 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engall.html |title=English Clubs Divisional Movements 1888–2016 |last1=Ross |first1=James |last2=Heneghan |first2=Michael |last3=Orford |first3=Stuart |last4=Culliton |first4=Eoin |date=25 Aug 2016 |website=[[RSSSF|Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]] |access-date=22 Jun 2023 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230622041929/https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engall.html |archive-date=22 Jun 2023}}</ref> In addition to the [[2022–23 Premier League|domestic league]], Arsenal also participated in this season's editions of the [[2022–23 FA Cup|FA Cup]], [[2022–23 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] and [[2022–23 UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League]], the latter of which was their [[Arsenal F.C. in European football|37th European campaign]].

Managed by [[Mikel Arteta]] in his third full season, Arsenal were the second-youngest team in the Premier League with an average starting age of 25 years and 52 days.<ref name="youngest teams BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/ckvz53jp82po |title=Who had the youngest average starting XI? |date=31 May 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=1 Jun 2023 |archive-date=31 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230531215322/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/ckvz53jp82po |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="season statistics AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/games-goals-and-records-202223-numbers |title=Games, goals and records: 2022/23 in numbers |last=James |first=Josh |date=31 May 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=1 Jun 2023 |archive-date=31 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230531093750/https://www.arsenal.com/news/games-goals-and-records-202223-numbers |url-status=live}}</ref> Following eliminations from the FA Cup, EFL Cup and UEFA Europa League, they finished second in the Premier League and qualified for next season's [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] after a six-year absence.

The season covers the period from 1 July 2022 to 30 June 2023. Notably, the fixture dates of domestic and European competitions were altered to accommodate the [[2022 FIFA World Cup|FIFA World Cup]] played in November and December 2022 in Qatar.

==Review==
===Background===
On 20 December 2019, Arsenal appointed former club [[Captain (association football)|captain]] [[Mikel Arteta]] – who was 37 years old then and had never managed before – as the new head coach on a three-and-a-half-year deal.<ref name="Arteta appointed as head coach AFC"/><ref name="Arteta appointed as head coach BBC"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/50873691 |title=Mikel Arteta: Arsenal manager insists he is ready and calls for new energy |date=20 Dec 2019 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=30 Jun 2022 |archive-date=16 Oct 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221016011321/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/50873691 |url-status=live}}</ref> The [[2019–20 Arsenal F.C. season|2019–20 season]] had been defined by a three-month lull between March and June, caused by the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]; and when it returned, it was [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/1645173 |title=Premier League, FA, EFL and WSL unite to postpone fixtures |date=13 Mar 2020 |website=Premier League |access-date=30 Jun 2022 |archive-date=4 Aug 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200804144759/https://www.premierleague.com/news/1645173 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/52833725 |title=Premier League set to restart on 17 June with Man City v Arsenal and Villa v Sheff Utd |last1=Roan |first1=Dan |last2=Stone |first2=Simon |last3=Scott |first3=Laura |date=28 May 2020 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=30 Jun 2022 |archive-date=29 May 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200529083550/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/52833725 |url-status=live}}</ref> The Gunners finished the league season in eighth place – far from a European qualification spot; but they earned a record-extending [[2020 FA Cup Final|14th FA Cup]] win on 1 August 2020, helping them qualify for next season's Europa League, and making Arteta the first person to win the FA Cup as both captain and coach of the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53546100 |title=FA Cup final 2020 Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea – Aubameyang double secures victory |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=1 Aug 2020 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=1 Jul 2022 |archive-date=8 Aug 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200808192923/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53546100 |url-status=live}}</ref>

The [[2020–21 Arsenal F.C. season|2020–21 season]] was heavily affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, as lots of domestic and European games were played behind closed doors. After Arsenal triumphed in the [[2020 FA Community Shield]], Arteta's title was changed to [[Manager (association football)|manager]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/arsenal/story/4178032/arsenal-change-arteta-to-manager-from-coach-as-part-of-restructuring-at-club |title=Arsenal change Arteta to manager from coach as part of restructuring at club |last=Olley |first=James |date=10 Sep 2020 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=30 Jun 2022 |archive-date=14 Jan 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210114085210/https://www.espn.com/soccer/arsenal/story/4178032/arsenal-change-arteta-to-manager-from-coach-as-part-of-restructuring-at-club |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Arteta's title changed to manager SkySports"/> On 26 December 2020, the Gunners recorded an important victory at home against Chelsea to end their seven-game run without a win in the Premier League and relieve the pressure on Arteta.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/55373755 |title=Arsenal 3-1 Chelsea: Gunners end winless run in Premier League |last=Bysouth |first=Alex |date=26 Dec 2020 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=1 Jul 2022 |archive-date=7 Feb 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210207223833/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/55373755 |url-status=live}}</ref> On 18 April 2021, Arsenal were announced as a founding club of the breakaway European competition [[European Super League|The Super League]]; they withdrew from the competition two days later amid near-universal condemnation.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/open-letter-our-fans |title=An open letter to our fans |date=20 Apr 2021 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=1 Jul 2022 |archive-date=4 Apr 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230404042803/https://www.arsenal.com/news/open-letter-our-fans |url-status=live}}</ref> The Gunners finished the season in eighth place once again, this time not qualifying for a European competition for the first time in 25 years.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/57132109 |title=Arsenal 2-0 Brighton: Nicolas Pepe scores double for Gunners |last=Collins |first=Ben |date=23 May 2021 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=1 Jul 2022 |archive-date=27 Jul 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220727132414/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/57132109 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/tottenham-europa-conference-league-premier-league-results-2020-21-b936770.html |title=Tottenham seal Europa Conference League spot; Arsenal miss out on European football for first time in 25 years |last=Muro |first=Giuseppe |date=23 May 2021 |website=[[Evening Standard]] |access-date=1 Jul 2022 |archive-date=27 Jul 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220727131521/https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/tottenham-europa-conference-league-premier-league-results-2020-21-b936770.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Pre-season===
[[File:Arsenal v Everton - 52223349030.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Arsenal captain Ødegaard (left) with Everton captain Jordan Pickford (right) ahead of Arsenal's pre-season friendly with Everton]]

It was reported on 29 June 2022 that the first-team players who were not in action for their respective countries since the end of the previous campaign were back to the [[Arsenal Training Centre|London Colney training ground]] for pre-season training.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/gallery-boys-are-back |title=📸 Gallery: The boys are back! |date=29 Jun 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=30 Jun 2022 |archive-date=29 Jun 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220629171817/https://www.arsenal.com/news/gallery-boys-are-back |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 4 July, the Gunners travelled to Germany for a small training camp at [[Adidas]] headquarters in [[Herzogenaurach]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/pre-season-heats-germany |title=📸 Pre-season heats up in Germany |date=6 Jul 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=7 Jul 2022 |archive-date=6 Jul 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220706103807/https://www.arsenal.com/news/pre-season-heats-germany |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-get-work-germany-training-camp |title=Arsenal get to work in Germany training camp |date=7 Jul 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=8 Jul 2022 |archive-date=8 Jul 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220708043146/https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-get-work-germany-training-camp |url-status=live}}</ref> Five academy players – [[Salah-Eddine Oulad M'Hand]], [[Charlie Patino]], [[Matt Smith (footballer, born 2000)|Matt Smith]], [[Lino Sousa]] and [[Reuell Walters]] – were with the first-team squad.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/find-out-about-our-young-gunners-germany |title=Find out about our young Gunners in Germany |last=Gilbert |first=Samuel |date=8 Jul 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=9 Jul 2022 |archive-date=8 Jul 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220708215848/https://www.arsenal.com/news/find-out-about-our-young-gunners-germany |url-status=live}}</ref>

Four days later, Arsenal faced [[2. Bundesliga]] side [[1. FC Nürnberg]] at [[Max-Morlock-Stadion]] in [[Nuremberg]]. New signings [[Gabriel Jesus]], [[Marquinhos (footballer, born 2003)|Marquinhos]] and [[Matt Turner (soccer)|Matt Turner]] made their non-competitive debuts for the club in a 5–3 win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/gabriel-jesus-pre-season-friendly-fc-nurnberg-match-report |title=Match report: 1. FC Nurnberg 3-5 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=8 Jul 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=9 Jul 2022 |archive-date=9 Jul 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220709000024/https://www.arsenal.com/gabriel-jesus-pre-season-friendly-fc-nurnberg-match-report |url-status=live}}</ref> They returned to England on the next day.

On 11 July, Arsenal confirmed that the internationals who were in action for their respective countries in June were all back to London Colney.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/internationals-return-london-colney |title=📸 Internationals return to London Colney |date=11 Jul 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=12 Jul 2022 |archive-date=11 Jul 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220711172406/https://www.arsenal.com/news/internationals-return-london-colney |url-status=live}}</ref> Two days later, manager Arteta named a 33-man squad for the trip to the United States where they would play three more friendlies. The 17-year-old defender Reuell Walters was the only academy player to travel with the first team to the US.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/squad-named-us-tour |title=Squad named for US tou |last=James |first=Josh |date=13 Jul 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=14 Jul 2022 |archive-date=14 Jul 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220714000126/https://www.arsenal.com/news/squad-named-us-tour |url-status=live}}</ref>

The Gunners faced fellow Premier League side [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] at [[M&T Bank Stadium]] in [[Baltimore]], Maryland on 16 July. Gabriel Jesus and [[Bukayo Saka]] both scored one goal in the first half, helping the team win 2–0.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Jul-16/arsenal-2-0-everton-match-report |title=Match report: Arsenal 2-0 Everton |last=James |first=Josh |date=17 Jul 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=18 Jul 2022 |archive-date=17 Jul 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220717025407/https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Jul-16/arsenal-2-0-everton-match-report |url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Arsenal took on [[Major League Soccer]] side [[Orlando City SC|Orlando City]] at [[Exploria Stadium]] in [[Orlando, Florida|Orlando]], Florida. The Gunners won 3–1 with [[Gabriel Martinelli]] scoring the opener, [[Eddie Nketiah]] scoring the second, and [[Reiss Nelson]] scoring the third.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Jul-20/orlando-city-arsenal-match-report |title=Match report: Orlando City 1-3 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=21 Jul 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=22 Jul 2022 |archive-date=21 Jul 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220721063637/https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Jul-20/orlando-city-arsenal-match-report |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 23 July, the club played their third and final game of the USA tour – also the final game of the [[2022 Florida Cup]] series – against Premier League side [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] at [[Camping World Stadium]] in Orlando. New signing [[Oleksandr Zinchenko (footballer)|Oleksandr Zinchenko]] made his non-competitive debut for Arsenal. In the 15th minute, Gabriel Jesus put the Gunners ahead with his fourth goal of pre-season. On 36 minutes, [[Martin Ødegaard]] added a further goal by sliding his shot low into the net. Saka scored the third shortly after the hour mark. [[Albert Sambi Lokonga]] headed in a cross from [[Cédric Soares]] at the far post in the closing stages, making the score 4–0. Arsenal ended the 10-day trip to America with winning the Florida Cup.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/chelsea-match-report-pre-season-friendly-america-jesus-odegaard |title=Match report: Arsenal 4-0 Chelsea |last=James |first=Josh |date=24 Jul 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=25 Jul 2022 |archive-date=24 Jul 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220724052813/https://www.arsenal.com/chelsea-match-report-pre-season-friendly-america-jesus-odegaard |url-status=live}}</ref>

The Gunners finished their pre-season campaign by thrashing [[La Liga]] side [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] 6–0 to claim the [[2022 Emirates Cup]] on 30 July. The match saw four goals in the opening 20 minutes, courtesy of braces from Saka and Gabriel Jesus, with the Brazilian completing his treble on 77 minutes before Nketiah netted in the final minute.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Jul-30/arsenal-6-0-sevilla-fc-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 6-0 Sevilla |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=30 Jul 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=31 Jul 2022 |archive-date=30 Jul 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220730232033/https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Jul-30/arsenal-6-0-sevilla-fc-match-report |url-status=live}}</ref>

Before the start of the game against Sevilla, Arsenal announced that Ødegaard was named their new men's first-team [[Captain (association football)|captain]].<ref name="Ødegaard named captain AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/martin-odegaard-named-captain |title=Martin Odegaard named captain |date=30 Jul 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=31 Jul 2022 |archive-date=30 Jul 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220730100409/https://www.arsenal.com/news/martin-odegaard-named-captain |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/arsenal-announce-odegaard-new-captain/blt6820675da9ef3714 |title=Arsenal announce Odegaard is their new captain |last=Darwin |first=Stephen |date=30 Jul 2022 |website=Goal |access-date=31 Jul 2022 |archive-date=30 Jul 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220730152412/https://www.goal.com/en/news/arsenal-announce-odegaard-new-captain/blt6820675da9ef3714 |url-status=live}}</ref>

====First-team transfers (summer transfer window)====
[[File:Lens - Marseille (22-01-2022) 15.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Saliba with Marseille in January 2022]]

In the previous season, French centre-back [[William Saliba]] spent a year on loan with [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] in [[Ligue 1]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/william-saliba-joins-marseille-loan |title=William Saliba joins Marseille on loan |date=15 Jul 2021 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=23 May 2022 |archive-date=16 Jul 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210716074739/https://www.arsenal.com/news/william-saliba-joins-marseille-loan |url-status=live}}</ref> During his time with Marseille, Saliba made 52 appearances in all competitions, and helped the club to second in the league, whilst also reaching the semi-finals of the inaugural [[2021–22 UEFA Europa Conference League|Europa Conference League season]]. Saliba was named as [[Ligue 1 Young player of the year|Ligue 1 Young Player of the Year]] and was awarded a position in the [[Trophées UNFP du football#Team of the Year|Team of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/saliba-named-unfp-ligue-1-young-player-year |title=Saliba named UNFP Ligue 1 Young Player of the Year |last=Small |first=Aidan |date=16 May 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=23 May 2022 |archive-date=23 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220523143143/https://www.arsenal.com/news/saliba-named-unfp-ligue-1-young-player-year |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/L-equipe-type-de-la-saison-de-ligue-1-aux-trophees-unfp-avec-un-trio-d-attaque-terrier-ben-yedder-mbappe/1333260 |title=L'équipe type de la saison de Ligue 1 aux trophées UNFP avec un trio d'attaque Terrier-Ben Yedder-Mbappé |date=15 May 2022 |website=[[L'Équipe]] |access-date=23 May 2022 |language=fr |trans-title=The team of the Ligue 1 season at the UNFP trophies with an attacking trio Terrier-Ben Yedder-Mbappé |archive-date=1 Jun 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220601035838/https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/L-equipe-type-de-la-saison-de-ligue-1-aux-trophees-unfp-avec-un-trio-d-attaque-terrier-ben-yedder-mbappe/1333260 |url-status=live}}</ref> He also won his first caps for France.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Benjamin-pavard-bayern-forfait-william-saliba-om-appele-en-equipe-de-france/1323576 |title=Benjamin Pavard (Bayern) forfait, William Saliba (OM) appelé en équipe de France |date=22 Mar 2022 |website=L'Équipe |access-date=23 May 2022 |language=fr |trans-title=Benjamin Pavard (Bayern) forfeited, William Saliba (OM) called up to the France team |archive-date=25 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220525035636/https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Benjamin-pavard-bayern-forfait-william-saliba-om-appele-en-equipe-de-france/1323576 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Saliba confirmed return TA">{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4175788/2022/06/05/william-saliba-confirms-return-to-arsenal-next-season-i-will-be-back/ |title=William Saliba confirms return to Arsenal next season — 'I will be back' |last1=Whitehead |first1=Jacob |last2=McNicholas |first2=James |date=6 Jun 2022 |website=The Athletic |access-date=8 Jun 2022 |archive-date=9 Jun 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220609125144/https://theathletic.com/news/william-saliba-return-arsenal/s9OLtimfEjg8/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In early June 2022, Saliba confirmed he would return to [[north London]] from his Marseille loan spell.<ref name="Saliba confirmed return TA"/> He would wear the number 12 shirt from the 2022–23 season.

On 19 May 2022, three days before the last game of the 2021–22 season, Arsenal announced that Greek defender [[Konstantinos Mavropanos]] joined [[Bundesliga]] side [[VfB Stuttgart]] on a permanent transfer.<ref name="Mavropanos departed"/> On 24 May, the club confirmed that Egyptian midfielder [[Mohamed Elneny]] had signed a new contract.<ref name="Elneny signed new contract 1 AFC"/><ref name="Elneny signed new contract 1 BBC"/> On 10 June, Arsenal announced that they were to release nine players, two of whom, [[Alexandre Lacazette]] and Nketiah, made men's first-team appearances for the Gunners.<ref name="Retained List"/> Eight days later, the club confirmed English striker and academy graduate Nketiah signed a new long-term contract, and would wear the number 14 shirt from the 2022–23 season, having previously worn the number 30.<ref name="Nketiah signed new contract AFC"/><ref name="Nketiah signed new contract BBC"/> The departure of French midfielder [[Matteo Guendouzi]] to Ligue 1 side Marseille was announced on 1 July.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/matteo-guendouzi-joins-olympique-marseille |title=Matteo Guendouzi joins Olympique Marseille |date=1 Jul 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=2 Jul 2022 |archive-date=1 Jul 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220701193212/https://www.arsenal.com/news/matteo-guendouzi-joins-olympique-marseille |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Guendouzi joined Marseille"/> Two weeks later, the Gunners confirmed American defender [[Auston Trusty]] joined [[EFL Championship]] side [[Birmingham City F.C.]] on a season-long loan.<ref name="Trusty on loan"/>

Arsenal announced their first signing of the summer transfer window on 10 June, with 19-year-old Brazilian forward Marquinhos joining the club on a long-term contract from [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Série A]] side [[São Paulo FC|São Paulo]].<ref name="Marquinhos joined"/><ref name="Marquinhos ESPN"/> Eleven days later, the club announced the signing of 22-year-old Portuguese midfielder [[Fábio Vieira (footballer, born 2000)|Fábio Vieira]] from [[Primeira Liga]] side [[FC Porto|Porto]]. He was given the number 21 shirt.<ref name="Vieira joined"/>

On 27 June, the Gunners confirmed that 28-year-old American goalkeeper Matt Turner had joined the club from [[Major League Soccer]] side [[New England Revolution]], and would wear the number 30 shirt.<ref name="Turner joined"/><ref name="Matt Turner BBC"/> As of June 2022, Turner had made 18 appearances for the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]].<ref name="Turner joined"/><ref name="Matt Turner BBC"/> He wore the number one shirt and played every game as USA won the [[2021 CONCACAF Gold Cup]] as hosts, keeping five [[clean sheet]]s in the tournament, and earning the [[CONCACAF Gold Cup awards#Best Goalkeeper|Golden Glove award]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.concacaf.com/gold-cup/article/matt-turner-of-u-s-named-winner-of-best-gk-award/ |title=Matt Turner of U.S. named winner of Best GK Award |date=2 Aug 2021 |website=[[CONCACAF]] |access-date=28 Jun 2022 |archive-date=30 Nov 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221130172805/https://www.concacaf.com/gold-cup/article/matt-turner-of-u-s-named-winner-of-best-gk-award/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2021/12/making-the-case-matt-turner-for-biosteel-us-soccer-male-player-of-the-year |title=MAKING THE CASE: Matt Turner for BioSteel U.S. Soccer Male Player of the Year |date=12 Dec 2021 |website=[[United States Soccer Federation]] |access-date=28 Jun 2022 |archive-date=2 Jul 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220702135928/https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2021/12/making-the-case-matt-turner-for-biosteel-us-soccer-male-player-of-the-year |url-status=live}}</ref> He was also honoured as [[MLS Goalkeeper of the Year Award|MLS Goalkeeper of the Year]] in 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/new-england-revolution-s-matt-turner-voted-2021-allstate-mls-goalkeeper-of-the-y |title=New England Revolution's Matt Turner Voted 2021 Allstate MLS Goalkeeper of the Year |date=22 Nov 2021 |website=[[Major League Soccer]] |access-date=28 Jun 2022 |archive-date=22 Dec 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221222170409/https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/new-england-revolution-s-matt-turner-voted-2021-allstate-mls-goalkeeper-of-the-y |url-status=live}}</ref> Turner has been an [[Arsenal F.C. supporters|Arsenal fan]] since his teenage years.<ref name="Matt Turner BBC"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/turner-im-really-really-excited-be-here |title=Turner – I'm really, really excited to be here |date=27 Jun 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=28 Jun 2022 |archive-date=27 Jun 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220627155340/https://www.arsenal.com/news/turner-im-really-really-excited-be-here |url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Gabriel Jesus fala sobre eliminação do Manchester City Aprendizado 0-2 screenshot.png|thumb|left|150px|Jesus with Manchester City in 2018]]
[[File:Zinchenko 2018.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Zinchenko playing for Manchester City in 2018]]

In July 2022, the Gunners announced two signings of notable players from fellow Premier League side [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], where Arteta spent three years and a half at as an assistant coach to [[Pep Guardiola]] before returning to Arsenal as head coach.<ref name="Arteta appointed as head coach AFC"/><ref name="Arteta appointed as head coach BBC"/> On 4 July, 25-year-old Brazilian striker Gabriel Jesus joined Arsenal on a long-term contract, and was assigned the number 9 shirt.<ref name="Jesus joined"/><ref name="Gabriel Jesus BBC"/> With the ability to play in several attacking positions, he is one of the leading strikers in the Premier League during his six seasons in Manchester City.<ref name="Jesus joined"/><ref name="Jesus joined 2">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arteta-gives-insight-jesus-qualities |title=Arteta gives insight into Jesus' qualities |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=4 Jul 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=5 Jul 2022 |archive-date=4 Jul 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220704141854/https://www.arsenal.com/news/arteta-gives-insight-jesus-qualities |url-status=live}}</ref> On 22 July, 25-year-old Ukrainian left-sided player and Arsenal supporter Oleksandr Zinchenko, who is comfortable operating in midfield and defence, joined the club on a long-term contract,<ref name="Zinchenko joined"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/oleksandr-zinchenko-interview-transfer |title='This is a dream come true' |last=James |first=Josh |date=22 Jul 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=23 Jul 2022 |archive-date=22 Jul 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220722194121/https://www.arsenal.com/oleksandr-zinchenko-interview-transfer |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Zinchenko BBC"/> and would wear the number 35 shirt. Gabriel Jesus and Zinchenko had both won four Premier League titles, the FA Cup and a number of EFL Cups as Manchester City players.<ref name="Jesus joined"/><ref name="Zinchenko joined"/> Manager Arteta believed that Gabriel Jesus and Zinchenko would help bring a winning mentality to the young squad.<ref name="Jesus joined 2"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/arteta-zinchenko-interview-transfer |title=Arteta – Alex is a unique footballer |last=James |first=Josh |date=22 Jul 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=23 Jul 2022 |archive-date=22 Jul 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220722194127/https://www.arsenal.com/arteta-zinchenko-interview-transfer |url-status=live}}</ref>

The Gunners continued their summer exodus after signing five players. In late July, the club announced the loan departures of English goalkeeper and academy graduate [[Arthur Okonkwo]] and Portuguese defender [[Nuno Tavares]] to [[EFL League Two|League Two]] side [[Crewe Alexandra F.C.|Crewe Alexandra]] and Ligue 1 side Marseille respectively.<ref name="Arthur Okonkwo on loan"/><ref name="Tavares on loan"/>

On 2 August, Arsenal announced German goalkeeper [[Bernd Leno]], who had made 125 appearances for the club in all competitions, joined fellow Premier League side [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] on a permanent transfer.<ref name="Leno departed"/><ref name="Leno departed 2"/> On the next day, the Gunners confirmed English goalkeeper [[Aaron Ramsdale]] took the number one shirt, moving from his previous number 32 following Leno's move to Fulham.<ref name="Ramsdale took number 1 shirt"/>

The departures of five first-team players were announced afterwards, as English forward and academy graduate [[Folarin Balogun]] joined Ligue 1 side [[Stade de Reims|Reims]] on a one-year loan,<ref name="Balogun on loan"/> Uruguayan midfielder [[Lucas Torreira]] completed his transfer to [[Süper Lig]] side [[Galatasaray S.K.|Galatasaray]],<ref name="Torreira departed"/> Spanish defender [[Pablo Marí]] joined [[Serie A]] side [[AC Monza]] on a one-year loan deal,<ref name="Marí on loan"/> Icelandic goalkeeper [[Rúnar Alex Rúnarsson]] joined Süper Lig side [[Alanyaspor]] on loan for the 2022–23 season,<ref name="Rúnarsson on loan"/> and Ivorian winger [[Nicolas Pépé]] joined Ligue 1 side [[OGC Nice]] on a season-long loan.<ref name="Pépé on loan"/>

On transfer deadline day, 1 September, two first-team players departed the club. English midfielder and academy graduate [[Ainsley Maitland-Niles]] joined fellow Premier League side [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] on a one-year loan.<ref name="Maitland-Niles on loan"/> Spanish defender and academy graduate [[Héctor Bellerín]], who had made 239 first-team appearances in all competitions and won three FA Cups with the club, joined La Liga side [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] on a permanent transfer.<ref name="Bellerin departed"/>

After the summer [[transfer window]] closed, there were twenty-four players in the first-team squad: three goalkeepers, eight defenders, six midfielders, and seven forwards. Eight first-team players were out on loan.<ref name="first-team squad (September) AFC"/>

===August===
The team began their campaign with a [[London derbies|London derby]] away against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] at [[Selhurst Park]], managed by former [[List of Arsenal F.C. players#Captains|Arsenal captain]] [[Patrick Vieira]]. Returning loanee Saliba and new signings Gabriel Jesus and Zinchenko made their competitive debuts for the team in a 2–0 win.<ref name="CRY v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/74911 |title=Crystal Palace v Arsenal, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=5 Aug 2022 |website=Premier League |access-date=6 Aug 2022 |archive-date=6 Aug 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220806051225/https://www.premierleague.com/match/74911 |url-status=live}}</ref> Martinelli opened the scoring in the 20th minute, becoming the first Brazilian to net a season-opening goal of a Premier League campaign.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/2722348 |title=Martinelli makes history with opening goal |date=5 Aug 2022 |website=Premier League |access-date=6 Aug 2022 |archive-date=6 Aug 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220806050328/https://www.premierleague.com/news/2722348 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="CRY v ARS PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62342936 |title=Crystal Palace 0-2 Arsenal: Gunners look 'hungry' after win, says Mikel Arteta |last=Bysouth |first=Alex |date=5 Aug 2022 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=6 Aug 2022 |archive-date=23 Aug 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230823211648/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62342936 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="CRY v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Aug-05/crystal-palace-0-2-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Crystal Palace 0-2 cross was deflected home by [[Marc Guéhi]] to ensure Arteta registered his 50th league victory,<ref name="CRY v ARS PL BBC"/> making him the second-quickest manager to reach 50 top-flight wins for Martinelli also scored in a 4–2 win.<ref name="ARS v LEI PL AFC"/><ref name="ARS v LEI PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62445691 |title=Arsenal 4-2 Leicester City: Gabriel |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220815163638/https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-leicester-city/report/464645 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 20 August, Arsenal faced newly-promoted [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] away at [[Dean Court]].<ref name="BOU v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/74931 |title=Bournemouth On 26 August, the draw for the [[2022–23 UEFA Europa League group stage|Europa League group stage]] was made. Arsenal were drawn in Group A, along with Dutch club [[PSV Eindhoven]], Norwegian champions [[FK Bodø/Glimt|Bodø/Glimt]] and Swiss champions [[FC Zürich|Zürich]].<ref name="Europa League group stage drawn AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/europa-league-group-stage-drawn |title=Europa League group stage drawn |date=26 Aug 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=27 Aug 2022 ===September===
The club started September with a 1–3 defeat at [[Old Trafford]] to [[Arsenal F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|rivals]] Manchester United on 4 September,<ref name="MUN v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/74966 |title=Man Utd v Arsenal, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=4 Sep 2022 |website=Premier League |access-date=5 Sep 2022 |archive-date=5 Sep 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220905024408/https://www.premierleague.com/match/74966 |url-status=live}}</ref> seeing their five-game winning start to the Premier League season come to an end. Zinchenko returned to the starting line-up, while Arsenal's first two defensive midfielders – Partey and Elneny – were still injured.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/team-news-zinchenko-returns-united-game |title=Team news: Zinchenko returns for United game |date=4 Sep 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=5 Sep 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="BRE v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/brentford-vs-arsenal/report/464706 |title=Brentford 0-3 Arsenal: Fabio Vieira scores first |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220918134143/http://www.skysports.com/football/brentford-vs-arsenal/report/464706 |url-status=live}}</ref> Vieira scored his first Premier League goal in a 3-0 win, with Saliba and Jesus also scoring two headers.<ref name="BRE v ARS PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62866738 |title=Brentford 0-3 Arsenal: Ethan Nwaneri becomes youngest ever Premier League player as Gunners go top |last=Johnston |first=Neil |date=18 Sep 2022 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=19 Sep 2022 |archive-date=29 Sep 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929163607/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62866738 |url-status=live}}</ref> As a schoolboy midfielder at the age of 15 years and 181 days, [[Ethan Nwaneri]] came off the bench to replace Vieira in second-half stoppage time. He became the [[Premier League records and statistics#Player records|youngest player]] to ever appear in the Premier League<ref name="BRE v ARS PL BBC"/> – breaking the record previously held by [[Harvey Elliott]],<ref name="BRE v ARS PL SkySports"/> and the [[Football records and statistics in England#League|all-time English top-flight record]] held since August 1964 by former [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] goalkeeper [[Derek Forster]], by three days.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/ethan-nwaneri-arsenals-15-year-old-becomes-youngest-top-flight-player-v2ln00f9v |title=Ethan Nwaneri: Arsenal's 15-year-old becomes youngest top-flight player |last=Jacob |first=Gary |date=18 Sep 2022 |website=[[The Sunday Times]] |access-date=19 Sep 2022 |archive-date=29 Sep 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929145558/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/ethan-nwaneri-arsenals-15-year-old-becomes-youngest-top-flight-player-v2ln00f9v |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Nwaneri became youngest top-flight player AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/nwaneri-enters-record-books |title=Nwaneri enters the record books |last=James |first=Josh |date=20 Sep 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=20 Sep 2022 |archive-date=20 Sep 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220920112808/https://www.arsenal.com/news/nwaneri-enters-record-books |url-status=live}}</ref> He also became [[List of Arsenal F.C. records and statistics#Player records|Arsenal's youngest-ever player]] in any senior competition, breaking the previous record of 16 years and 177 days, set by Cesc Fàbregas in the [[2003–04 Football League Cup|2003–04 League Cup]].<ref name="Nwaneri became youngest top-flight player AFC"/>

On 29 September, Arsenal announced that academy graduate [[Emile Smith Rowe]] had undergone surgery to repair a damaged tendon in his groin. He would return to full training in December.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/emile-smith-rowe-undergoes-surgery |title=Emile Smith Rowe undergoes surgery |date=29 Sep 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=30 Sep 2022 |archive-date=29 Sep 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929200829/https://www.arsenal.com/news/emile-smith-rowe-undergoes-surgery |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Smith Rowe underwent surgery BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63071309 |title=Emile Smith Rowe: Arsenal midfielder sidelined after groin operation |date=29 Sep 2022 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=30 Sep 2022 |archive-date=30 Sep 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220930064825/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63071309 |url-status=live}}</ref>

===October===
On 1 October, following the international break, the club played the [[North London derby]] at home against Tottenham.<ref name="ARS v TOT PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/74991 |title=Arsenal v Spurs, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=1 Oct 2022 |website=Premier League |access-date=2 Oct 2022 |archive-date=2 Oct 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221002005808/https://www.premierleague.com/match/74991 |url-status=live}}</ref> Partey opened the scoring in the 20th minute with a shot from 25 yards, the first time he had scored from outside the box in 65 attempts for Arsenal.<ref name="ARS v TOT PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/premier-league-match-report-tottenham-north-london-derby-emirates-stadium |title=Report: Arsenal 3-1 Tottenham Hotspur |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=1 Oct 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=2 Oct 2022 |archive-date=1 Oct 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221001150543/https://www.arsenal.com/premier-league-match-report-tottenham-north-london-derby-emirates-stadium |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="ARS v TOT PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-tottenham-hotspur/report/464715 |title=Arsenal 3-1 Tottenham: Granit Xhaka strike caps commanding victory as Gunners move four points clear |last=Wright |first=Nick |date=2 Oct 2022 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=2 Oct 2022 |archive-date=2 Oct 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221002035408/https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-tottenham-hotspur/report/464715 |url-status=live}}</ref> Although Spurs equalised in the 31st minute from a [[Harry Kane]] penalty, Jesus and Xhaka scored in the second half to take a 3-1 victory.<ref name="ARS v TOT PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63017880 |title=Arsenal 3-1 Tottenham: Gunners beat 10-man rivals to extend lead at top of Premier League |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=1 Oct 2022 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=2 Oct 2022 |archive-date=14 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230114020807/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63017880 |url-status=live}}</ref> The win kept Arsenal on top of the Premier League table, and meant that it was the first time the club had won three consecutive league home games against their rivals since September 2013.<ref name="ARS v TOT PL AFC"/><ref name="ARS v TOT PL SkySports"/> A Europa League game against [[FK Bodø/Glimt|Bodø/Glimt]], the defending [[2021 Eliteserien|Eliteserien]] champions, followed on 6 October at home.<ref name="ARS v BOD UEFA">{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2035958--arsenal-vs-bodo-glimt/ |title=Arsenal-Bodø/Glimt {{pipe}} UEFA Europa League 2022/23 |date=6 Oct 2022 |website=UEFA |access-date=7 Oct 2022 |archive-date=6 Oct 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221006205119/https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2035958--arsenal-vs-bodo-glimt/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Arsenal won 3–0, sending them top of their Europa League group.<ref name="ARS v BOD SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-bodo-glimt/report/477478 |title=Arsenal 3-0 Bodo/Glimt: Eddie Nketiah, Rob Holding and Fabio Vieira score to put Gunners top of Europa League group |last=Blitz |first=Sam |date=7 Oct 2022 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=7 Oct 2022 |archive-date=6 Oct 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221006225605/https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-bodo-glimt/report/477478 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="ARS v BOD AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Oct-06/arsenal-3-0-fk-bodo-glimt-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 3-0 Bodo/Glimt |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=6 Oct 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=7 Oct 2022 |archive-date=6 Oct 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221006233704/https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Oct-06/arsenal-3-0-fk-bodo-glimt-match-report |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="ARS v BOD BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63151667 |title=Arsenal 3-0 Bodo/Glimt: Arsenal ease to victory over Bodo/Glimt |last=Sanders |first=Emma |date=6 Oct 2022 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=7 Oct 2022 |archive-date=7 Oct 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221007075957/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63151667 On 9 October, the club faced ninth-placed Liverpool,<ref name="ARS v LIV PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75001 |title=Arsenal v Liverpool, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=9 Oct 2022 |website=Premier League |access-date=10 Oct 2022 |archive-date=8 Oct 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221008092148/https://www.premierleague.com/match/75001 |url-status=live}}</ref> a team that Arsenal had only won one of their last 14 Premier League matches against since the [[2015–16 Arsenal F.C. season|2015–16 season]] and had failed to score in their past six meetings with in all competitions.<ref name="Preview ARS v LIV PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/preview-arsenal-v-liverpool |title=Preview: Arsenal v Liverpool |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=8 Oct 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=10 Oct 2022 |archive-date=8 Oct 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221008103635/https://www.arsenal.com/news/preview-arsenal-v-liverpool |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="ARS v LIV PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-liverpool/report/464725 |title=Arsenal 3-2 Liverpool: Bukayo Saka and Gabriel Martinelli on target as Gunners return top of Premier League |last=Smith |first=Peter |date=9 Oct 2022 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=10 Oct 2022 |archive-date=10 Oct 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221010042538/https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-liverpool/report/464725 |url-status=live}}</ref> The Gunners took the lead after just 58 seconds when Martinelli tucked the ball home,<ref name="ARS v LIV PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Oct-09/arsenal-3-2-liverpool-match |title=Report: Arsenal 3-2 Liverpool |last=James |first=Josh |date=9 Oct 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=10 Oct 2022 |archive-date=9 Oct 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221009215232/https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Oct-09/arsenal-3-2-liverpool-match |url-status=live}}</ref> but Liverpool equalised through [[Darwin Núñez]] in the 34th minute.<ref name="ARS v LIV PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63106170 |title=Arsenal 3-2 Liverpool: Bukayo Saka double helps Gunners regain top spot |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=9 Oct 2022 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=10 Oct 2022 |archive-date=9 Oct 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221009210321/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63106170 |url-status=live}}</ref> Arsenal reclaimed the lead shortly before half-time through Saka, but Liverpool again got back on terms through substitute [[Roberto Firmino]] in the 53rd minute. Saka nevertheless scored a decisive penalty in the 76th minute, making the score 3–2,<ref name="ARS v LIV PL BBC"/><ref name="ARS v LIV PL SkySports"/> and sealing the Gunners' first win over Liverpool since July 2020.<ref name="Preview ARS v LIV PL AFC"/> Four days later, the Gunners faced Bodø/Glimt away.<ref name="BOD v ARS UEFA">{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2035959--bodo-glimt-vs-arsenal/ |title=Bodø/Glimt-Arsenal {{pipe}} UEFA Europa League 2022/23 |date=13 Oct 2022 |website=UEFA |access-date=14 Oct 2022 place on an [[Artificial turf|artificial pitch]] at [[Aspmyra Stadion]], where the Norwegian team had won each of their last 14 home matches in European competition.<ref name="BOD v ARS AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Oct-13/fk-bodo-glimt-0-1-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Bodo/Glimt 0-1 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=13 Oct 2022 |website=Arsenal FC AFC"/><ref name="BOD v ARS BBC"/><ref name="BOD v ARS SkySports"/>

Arsenal continued their league campaign on 16 October, facing 14th-placed [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] away at [[Elland Road]]. The game saw goalkeeper Ramsdale produce a man of the match display as the Gunners won 1–0.<ref name="LEE v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75014 |title=Leeds v Arsenal, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=16 Oct 2022 |website=Premier League |access-date=17 Oct 2022 |archive-date=17 Oct 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221017015300/https://www.premierleague.com/match/75014 |url-status=live}}</ref> Saka scored the winning goal from a tight angle in the 35th minute, assisted by Ødegaard; Leeds striker [[Patrick Bamford]] missed a penalty midway through the second half.<ref name="LEE v ARS PL SkySports"/><ref name="LEE v ARS PL BBC"/><ref name="LEE v ARS PL AFC"/> Having won nine of their first ten league games for the first time ever,<ref name="LEE v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Oct-16/leeds-0-1-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Leeds United 0-1 Arsenal |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=16 Oct 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=17 Oct 2022 |archive-date=16 Oct 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221016200555/https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Oct-16/leeds-0-1-arsenal-match-report |url-status=live}}</ref> Arsenal moved four points clear at the top of the league.<ref name="LEE v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/leeds-united-vs-arsenal/report/464738 |title=Leeds 0-1 Arsenal: Bukayo Saka keeps Gunners |archive-date=16 Oct 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221016191049/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63189783 |url-status=live}}</ref> On 20 October, the Gunners played the postponed Europa League match at home to Dutch side PSV Eindhoven.<ref name="ARS v PSV UEFA">{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2035955--arsenal-vs-psv/ |title=Arsenal-PSV {{pipe}} UEFA Europa League 2022/23 |date=20 Oct 2022 |website=UEFA |access-date=21 Oct 2022 |archive-date=21 Oct 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221021023708/https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2035955--arsenal-vs-psv/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Xhaka's 70th minute strike sealed a third-straight 1-0 victory.<ref name="ARS v PSV BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63319350 |title=Arsenal 1-0 PSV Eindhoven: Granit Xhaka scores the winner as hosts close in on last 16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221020235938/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63319350 |url-status=live}}</ref> The win ensured Arsenal qualified for the [[2022–23 UEFA Europa League knockout phase|Europa League knockout stage]] with two group games to spare.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-psv-eindhoven/report/477462 |title=Arsenal 1-0 PSV: ===November===
On 3 November, the Gunners hosted Swiss side Zürich at Emirates Stadium in their final Europa League group game.<ref name="ARS v ZUR UEFA">{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2035963--arsenal-vs-zurich/ |title=Arsenal-Zürich {{pipe}} UEFA Europa League 2022/23 |date=3 Nov 2022 |website=UEFA |access-date=4 Nov 2022 Tierney scored the only goal of the game with a left-footed shot from 20 yards to the bottom right corner, helping the team win 1–0.<ref name="ARS v ZUR AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/match-report-europa-league-fc-zurich-kieran-tierney-group-a |title=Report: Arsenal 1-0 FC Zurich |last=James |first=Josh |date=3 Nov 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |url-status=live}}</ref> They would go straight into the Europa League [[2022–23 UEFA Europa League knockout phase|round of 16]] in March 2023, skipping the knockout play-off round in February.<ref name="ARS v ZUR AFC"/><ref name="ARS v ZUR SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-fc-zurich/report/477526 |title=Arsenal 1-0 FC Zurich: Kieran Tierney's first goal of F.C. rivalry|rivals]] [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] on 6 November,<ref name="CHE v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75052 Gabriel Magalhães's close-range finish from Saka's corner in the 63rd minute earned the visitors a 1–0 win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63443732 |title=Chelsea 0-1 Arsenal: Three days later, the Gunners entered the [[2022–23 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] in the third round, facing Premier League side [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] at home.<ref name="ARS v BHA Estonia international keeper and academy graduate [[Karl Hein (footballer)|Karl Hein]] made his competitive debut for the first team and started in goal,<ref name="ARS v BHA EFLCup BBC"/><ref name="ARS v BHA EFLCup SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-brighton-and-hove-albion/477322 |title=Arsenal 1-3 Brighton: Seagulls hit back to claim victory in a Premier League side.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.err.ee/1608783904/karl-jakob-hein-s-arsenal-first-team-debut-ends-in-home-loss-to-brighton |title=Karl Jakob Hein's Arsenal first team debut Nketiah opened the scoring,<ref name="ARS v BHA EFLCup AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/carabao-cup-match-report-emirates-stadium-eddie-nketiah-mikel-arteta |title=Report: Arsenal 1-3 seasons that Arsenal had failed to progress past the third round of the [[EFL Cup]] (formerly League Cup).<ref name="ARS v BHA EFLCup SkySports"/> On 12 November, Arteta's side played their last game ===December===
On 4 December, manager Arteta named a 27-man squad – including thirteen academy players – for the trip to the United Arab Emirates, where they would play two friendlies in the Dubai Super Cup.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/squad-confirmed-dubai-super-cup |title=Squad confirmed for the Dubai Super Cup |date=4 Dec 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=5 Dec 2022 |archive-date=4 Dec 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221204155753/https://www.arsenal.com/news/squad-confirmed-dubai-super-cup |url-status=live}}</ref> Two days later, Arsenal confirmed that striker Gabriel Jesus had undergone surgery to his right knee after suffering an injury during Brazil's World Cup group stage match against Cameroon on 2 December. The club did not give any timescale on his return.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/gabriel-jesus-undergoes-surgery |title=Gabriel Jesus undergoes surgery |date=6 Dec 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=7 Dec 2022 |archive-date=6 Dec 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221206201643/https://www.arsenal.com/news/gabriel-jesus-undergoes-surgery |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Jesus underwent surgery BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63880482 |title=Gabriel Jesus: Arsenal and Brazil forward has successful surgery on knee injury |date=6 Dec 2022 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=7 Dec 2022 |archive-date=6 Dec 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221206221935/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63880482 |url-status=live}}</ref> The Gunners faced [[Ligue 1]] side [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] in Dubai on 8 December, winning 3-0.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Dec-08/arsenal-3-0-lyon-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 3-0 Lyon |last=James |first=Josh |date=8 Dec 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=9 Dec 2022 |archive-date=8 Dec 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221208234135/https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Dec-08/arsenal-3-0-lyon-match-report |url-status=live}}</ref> They played their second game in Dubai against [[Serie A]] side [[AC Milan|Milan]] on 13 December, winning 2-1 and claiming the Dubai Super Cup.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Dec-13/arsenal-2-1-ac-milan-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 2-1 AC Milan |last=James |first=Josh |date=13 Dec 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=14 Dec 2022 |archive-date=18 Dec 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221218172708/https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Dec-13/arsenal-2-1-ac-milan-match-report |url-status=live}}</ref> After flying back to England, Arsenal lost 2-0 to Serie A side [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in their final friendly at Emirates Stadium on 17 December.<ref name="ARS v JUV Friendly AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Dec-17/arsenal-0-2-juventus-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 0-2 Juventus |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=17 Dec 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=18 Dec 2022 |archive-date=17 Dec 2022 The Gunners' first league action after the World Cup was a [[Boxing Day]] fixture at home against 16th-placed West Ham United, on the anniversary of Arteta's first game as Arsenal manager.<ref name="ARS v WHU PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75071 |title=Arsenal v West Ham, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=26 Dec 2022 |website=Premier League |access-date=27 Dec FC |access-date=27 Dec 2022 |archive-date=26 Dec 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221226235457/https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Dec-26/arsenal-3-1-west-ham-united-match-report |url-status=live}}</ref>

On New Year's Eve, Arsenal travelled to the south coast of England to play their final game of 2022 – also the last Premier League fixture of the year – against 7th-placed Brighton & Hove Albion.<ref name="BHA v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75082 |title=Brighton v Arsenal, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=31 Dec 2022 |website=Premier League |access-date=1 Jan 2023 |archive-date=1 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230101065505/https://www.premierleague.com/match/75082 |url-status=live}}</ref> Before kick-off, there was a minute's applause in tribute to [[Pelé]], who had died on 29 December.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/42751517 |title=Pele: Brazil football legend dies aged 82 |date=29 Dec 2022 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=30 Dec 2022 |archive-date=29 Dec 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221229215920/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/42751517 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/2976447 |title=Premier League matches to feature tributes to Pele |date=30 Dec 2022 |website=Premier League |access-date=30 Dec 2022 |archive-date=29 Dec 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221229222059/https://www.premierleague.com/news/2976447 |url-status=live}}</ref> Goals from Saka, Ødegaard, and Nketiah put Arsenal three goals up, before Mitoma reduced the deficit for the Seagulls in the 65th minute.<ref name="BHA v ARS PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64083699 |title=Brighton & Hove Albion 2-4 Arsenal: Gunners extend lead to seven points |last=Oscroft |first=Tim |date=31 Dec 2022 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=1 Jan 2023 |archive-date=31 Dec 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221231235201/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64083699 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="BHA v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Dec-31/brighton-2-4-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Brighton & Hove Albion 2-4 Arsenal |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=31 Dec 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=1 Jan 2023 |archive-date=31 Dec 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221231230449/https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2022-Dec-31/brighton-2-4-arsenal-match-report |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="BHA v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/brighton-and-hove-albion-vs-arsenal/report/464806 |title=Brighton 2-4 Arsenal: Gunners move seven points clear after surviving late Seagulls rally |date=31 Dec 2022 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=1 Jan 2023 |archive-date=31 Dec 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221231203800/https://www.skysports.com/football/brighton-and-hove-albion-vs-arsenal/report/464806 |url-status=live}}</ref> Martinelli scored six minutes later, and although [[Evan Ferguson]] pulled a goal back, the 4-2 victory took Arsenal seven points clear at the top of the table, the fifth team in English top-flight history to pick up as many as 43 points from the first 16 games in a season.<ref name="BHA v ARS PL AFC"/><ref name="BHA v ARS PL BBC"/><ref name="BHA v ARS PL SkySports"/> Arteta picked up his second Premier League Manager of the Month award of the campaign, winning the award for the fourth time in his career.<ref name="Arteta named November/December's PL MOTM"/> Ødegaard won the Premier League Player of the Month award, the first Arsenal player to do so since [[Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang]] in September 2019.<ref name="Ødegaard named November/December's PL POTM"/> It was also the first time since March 2015 the club scooped both awards, when manager Arsène Wenger and striker [[Olivier Giroud]] were the recipients.<ref name="Arteta named November/December's PL MOTM"/>

===January===
Arsenal started 2023 with a home game against third-placed Newcastle on 3 January,<ref name="ARS v NEW PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75091 |title=Arsenal v Newcastle, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=3 Jan 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=4 Jan 2023 |archive-date=3 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230103152851/https://www.premierleague.com/match/75091 |url-status=live}}</ref> hoping to extend their advantage over Manchester City. However, neither team was able to break the deadlock and the game finished 0–0.<ref name="ARS v NEW PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64099600 |title=Arsenal 0-0 Newcastle United: Newcastle earn point against league-leaders Arsenal |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=3 Jan 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=4 Jan 2023 |archive-date=3 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230103224508/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64099600 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="ARS v NEW PL SkySports">{{cite web Sports |access-date=4 Jan 2023 |archive-date=3 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230103225557/https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-newcastle-united/report/464815 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-Jan-03/arsenal-0-0-newcastle-united-match-report |title=Match report: Arsenal 0-0 Newcastle United |last=James Gunners entered the [[2022–23 FA Cup|FA Cup]] in the third round, facing [[EFL League One|League One]] side [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]] away at [[Kassam Stadium]].<ref name="OXF v ARS FACup BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64203475 |title=Oxford United 0-3 Arsenal: Eddie Nketiah scores twice as Gunners progress |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=9 Jan 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=10 Jan 2023 |archive-date=9 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230109233341/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64203475 |url-status=live}}</ref> The opener came from Elneny and was followed by a brace from Nketiah, in a 3-0 win.<ref name="OXF v ARS FACup SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/oxford-united-vs-arsenal/report/479263 |title=Oxford 0-3 Arsenal: Eddie Nketiah double sets up fourth-round tie against Man City |last=Shread |first=Joe |date=9 Jan 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=10 Jan 2023 |archive-date=9 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230109231620/https://www.skysports.com/football/oxford-united-vs-arsenal/report/479263 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="OXF v ARS FACup AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-Jan-09/oxford-united-0-3-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Oxford United 0-3 Arsenal |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=9 Jan 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=10 Jan 2023 |archive-date=9 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230109233639/https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-Jan-09/oxford-united-0-3-arsenal-match-report |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="OXF v ARS FACup BBC"/> On 15 January, Arsenal faced rivals Tottenham at [[Tottenham Hotspur Stadium]] in the second [[North London derby]] of the season.<ref name="TOT v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75109 |title=Spurs v Arsenal, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=15 Jan 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=16 Jan 2023 |archive-date=16 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230116004553/https://www.premierleague.com/match/75109 |url-status=live}}</ref> Saka's cross was deflected home by Spurs goalkeeper Lloris in the 14th minute, while Ødegaard doubled Arsenal's lead with a long-range strike later in the first half.<ref name="TOT v ARS PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64201166 |title=Tottenham Hotspur 0 Arsenal 2: Hugo Lloris own goal and Martin Odegaard strike sends Gunners eight clear |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=15 Jan 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=16 Jan 2023 |archive-date=25 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230125091931/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64201166 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="TOT v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/match-report-premier-league-tottenham-north-london-derby |title=Report: Tottenham Hotspur 0-2 Arsenal |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=15 Jan 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=16 Jan 2023 |archive-date=15 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230115212411/https://www.arsenal.com/match-report-premier-league-tottenham-north-london-derby |url-status=live}}</ref> Arsenal keeper [[Aaron Ramsdale]] produced a man of the match display with seven saves, helping his side record the first clean sheet in North London derbies since Arteta took charge of Arsenal in December 2019.<ref name="TOT v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/tottenham-hotspur-vs-arsenal/report/464833 |title=Tottenham 0-2 Arsenal: Hugo Lloris own goal and Martin Odegaard stunner help Gunners go eight points clear |last=Wright |first=Nick |date=15 Jan 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=16 Jan 2023 |archive-date=16 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230116010400/https://www.skysports.com/football/tottenham-hotspur-vs-arsenal/report/464833 |url-status=live}}</ref> Having secured their first league double over Tottenham since the [[2013–14 Arsenal F.C. season|2013–14 season]],<ref name="TOT v ARS PL AFC"/><ref name="TOT v ARS PL SkySports"/> Arsenal moved eight points clear of City.<ref name="TOT v ARS PL BBC"/> An incident at the end of the game, in which Ramsdale was kicked in the back by a Tottenham supporter who had jumped onto the advertising hoarding, was strongly criticised by the [[Professional Footballers' Association]], the [[Football Association]], and the Premier League said: "There is no place in football for acts of violence, and under no circumstance should players be attacked or fear for their safety at games."<ref name="Ramsdale kicked by fan BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64285177 |title=Tottenham 0-2 Arsenal: Aaron Ramsdale attacked by |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11670/12787622/arsenal-goalkeeper-aaron-ramsdale-kicked-by-fan-after-2-0-win-at-tottenham-in-north-london-derby |title=Aaron Ramsdale kicked by spectator |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230116001257/https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/ramsdale-confirms-altercation-with-spurs-fan-after-derby-win-2023-01-15/ |archive-date=16 Jan 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/breaking-tottenham-fan-attacks-ramsdale-29240489 |title=Tottenham fan pleads guilty to attacking Arsenal's On 22 January, Arsenal faced [[Arsenal F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|rivals]] Manchester United,<ref name="ARS v MUN PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75111 |title=Arsenal v Man Utd, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=22 Jan 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=23 Jan 2023 |archive-date=22 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230122155918/https://www.premierleague.com/match/75111 |url-status=live}}</ref> the only team that had beaten them in the Premier League this season up until that point, at home.<ref name="Preview ARS v MUN PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/preview-arsenal-v-manchester-united |title=Preview: Arsenal v Manchester United |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=21 Jan 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=23 Jan 2023 |archive-date=23 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230123195858/https://www.arsenal.com/news/preview-arsenal-v-manchester-united |url-status=live}}</ref> In the 17th minute, Rashford gave United the lead with a long-range strike, but Nketiah levelled seven minutes later.<ref name="ARS v MUN PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64279776 |title=Arsenal 3-2 Manchester United: Late goal by Eddie Nketiah gives Arsenal win over United |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=22 Jan 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=23 Jan 2023 |archive-date=22 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230122190512/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64279776 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="ARS v MUN PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-manchester-united/report/464835 |title=Arsenal 3-2 Manchester United: Eddie Nketiah nets late winner as Gunners restore five-point Premier League lead |last=Morgan |first=Richard |date=22 Jan 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=23 Jan 2023 |archive-date=22 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230122222229/https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-manchester-united/report/464835 |url-status=live}}</ref> On 53 minutes, Saka cut in from the right and arrowed a shot across United goalkeeper David de Gea into the far corner of the goal,<ref name="ARS v MUN PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/match-report-manchester-united-premier-league-emirates-stadium |title=Report: Arsenal 3-2 Manchester United |last=James |first=Josh |date=22 Jan 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=23 Jan 2023 |archive-date=22 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230122202250/https://www.arsenal.com/match-report-manchester-united-premier-league-emirates-stadium |url-status=live}}</ref> before [[Lisandro Martínez]] looped a header into the net six minutes later.<ref name="ARS v MUN PL BBC"/> In the 90th minute, the ball came loose in the area and Nketiah was able to steer it home, sealing a 3-2 victory.<ref name="ARS v MUN PL SkySports"/><ref name="ARS v MUN PL BBC"/> The win gave the Gunners a five-point advantage at the top of the Premier League with a game in hand.<ref name="ARS v MUN PL BBC"/>

The Gunners headed to face Manchester City on 27 January at [[City of Manchester Stadium|Etihad Stadium]] in the [[2022–23 FA Cup|FA Cup]] fourth round.<ref name="MCI v ARS FACup BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64417476 |title=Manchester City 1-0 Arsenal: Nathan Ake scores decisive goal as hosts edge into FA Cup fifth round |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=27 Jan 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=28 Jan 2023 |archive-date=27 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230127225751/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64417476 |url-status=live}}</ref> New recruit Trossard was handed his first Arsenal start, and Kiwior was named on the bench following his signing with the club earlier in the week.<ref name="MCI v ARS FACup BBC"/> In the 64th minute, [[Nathan Aké]] scored the only goal of the tight game with a low shot, helping the hosts win 1–0.<ref name="MCI v ARS FACup SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/34651/12795030/man-city-1-0-arsenal-nathan-akes-second-half-strike-earns-pep-guardiolas-side-fa-cup-win-over-their-premier-league-title-rivals |title=Man City 1-0 Arsenal: Nathan Ake's second-half strike earns Pep Guardiola's side FA Cup win over their Premier League title rivals |last=Smith |first=Peter |date=27 Jan 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=28 Jan 2023 |archive-date=28 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230128043530/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/34651/12795030/man-city-1-0-arsenal-nathan-akes-second-half-strike-earns-pep-guardiolas-side-fa-cup-win-over-their-premier-league-title-rivals |url-status=live}}</ref> On 31 January, the club announced that midfielder Elneny had undergone surgery to his right knee after suffering a significant injury in a training session. He would be out for an extended period of time.<ref name="Elneny underwent surgery AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/medical-update-mohamed-elneny |title=Medical update: Mohamed Elneny |date=31 Jan 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=31 Jan 2023 |archive-date=31 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230131130713/https://www.arsenal.com/news/medical-update-mohamed-elneny |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Elneny underwent surgery BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64470830 |title=Mohamed Elneny: Arsenal midfielder out for 'extended period' after knee surgery |date=31 Jan 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=31 Jan 2023 |archive-date=31 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230131144931/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64470830 |url-status=live}}</ref> Arteta was named Premier League Manager of the Month for the third time in the season. He was the first manager to win the award in successive months since Manchester City's Guardiola did so in November and December 2021. Arteta also became the first Arsenal manager to win the award three times in a single campaign.<ref name="Arteta named January's PL MOTM"/>

====First-team transfers (winter transfer window)====

 | align = right
 | total_width = 300

 | image1 = Leandro Trossard 2022.jpg

On 16 January, the club confirmed English goalkeeper and academy graduate [[Arthur Okonkwo]] was recalled from his loan at [[EFL League Two|League Two]] side [[Crewe Alexandra F.C.|Crewe Alexandra]] and joined [[Austrian Football Bundesliga|Austrian Bundesliga]] side [[SK Sturm Graz|Sturm Graz]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref name="Arthur Okonkwo on loan 2"/> Arsenal announced their first signing of the winter transfer window on 20 January with 28-year-old Belgian forward Leandro Trossard joining the club on a long-term contract from fellow Premier League side Brighton & Hove Albion. He would wear the number 19 shirt.<ref name="Trossard joined"/><ref name="Leandro Trossard BBC"/> With the ability to play in several attacking positions, Trossard scored seven goals in sixteen Premier League games for Brighton this season. He also made three appearances for [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]] at the [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022 World Cup]].<ref name="Trossard joined"/><ref name="Leandro Trossard BBC"/>

On 23 January, the club confirmed that they had signed 22-year-old Polish defender [[Jakub Kiwior]] from [[Serie A]] side [[Spezia Calcio|Spezia]]. He would wear the number 15 shirt.<ref name="Kiwior joined"/><ref name="Jakub Kiwior BBC"/> A versatile defender, Kiwior was capable of playing both as a centre-back and as a defensive midfielder during his time with the Italian side.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/get-know-jakub-kiwior-these-fun-facts |title=Get to know Jakub Kiwior with these fun facts |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=23 Jan 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=24 Jan 2023 |archive-date=23 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230123235350/https://www.arsenal.com/news/get-know-jakub-kiwior-these-fun-facts |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2023/01/23/jakub-kiwior-might-prove-exactly-right-player-arsenal/ |title=A defender in the Italian mould – why Jakub Kiwior should prove the perfect player for Arsenal |last=Dean |first=Sam |date=23 Jan 2023 |website=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |access-date=24 Jan 2023 |archive-date=24 Jan 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230124013439/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2023/01/23/jakub-kiwior-might-prove-exactly-right-player-arsenal/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/arsenal-might-have-signed-their-thomas-partey-back-up-and-its-not-jorginho-jakub-kiwior-transfers-signings-gossip-rumours-afc |title=Arsenal have signed a potential Thomas Partey backup – and it's not Jorginho |last=White |first=Mark |date=31 Jan 2023 |website=[[FourFourTwo]] |access-date=1 Feb 2023 |archive-date=2 Feb 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230202020838/https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/arsenal-might-have-signed-their-thomas-partey-back-up-and-its-not-jorginho-jakub-kiwior-transfers-signings-gossip-rumours-afc |url-status=live}}</ref> As of December 2022, he had won nine caps for [[Poland national football team|Poland]] and started all four of their matches at the 2022 World Cup.<ref name="Kiwior joined"/><ref name="Jakub Kiwior BBC"/>

On transfer deadline day, 31 January, the Gunners announced that 31-year-old Italian midfielder [[Jorginho (footballer, born December 1991)|Jorginho]] had joined the club from Premier League side [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] and would wear the number 20 shirt.<ref name="Jorginho joined"/><ref name="Jorginho BBC"/> Jorginho had made 143 Premier League appearances for Chelsea, winning the UEFA Europa League, UEFA Champions League, [[UEFA Super Cup]] and [[FIFA Club World Cup]] during his time at the club. Capped 46 times, he was part of the [[Italy national football team|Italy]] squad which won [[UEFA Euro 2020]].<ref name="Jorginho joined"/><ref name="Jorginho BBC"/> In 2021, he was named [[UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award|UEFA Men's Player of the Year]] and placed third in the [[2021 Ballon d'Or|Ballon d'Or]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/026c-1317c5d44053-673457b2aa24-1000--men-s-player-of-the-year-jorginho/ |title=Jorginho wins UEFA Men's Player of the Year award |date=26 Aug 2021 |website=UEFA |access-date=31 Jan 2023 |archive-date=4 Feb 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230204201705/https://www.uefa.com/insideuefa/awards/news/026c-1317c5d44053-673457b2aa24-1000--men-s-player-of-the-year-jorginho/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59454640 |title=Ballon d'Or: Lionel Messi wins award as best player in world football for seventh time |date=29 Nov 2021 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=31 Jan 2023 |archive-date=2 Dec 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202042954/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59454640 |url-status=live}}</ref>

The departures of two first-team players were announced on the same day, as Brazilian forward Marquinhos joined [[EFL Championship]] side [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] on loan for the remainder of the season,<ref name="Marquinhos on loan"/> and Belgian midfielder [[Albert Sambi Lokonga]] joined fellow Premier League side [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] on loan until June 2023.<ref name="Sambi Lokonga on loan"/> On 1 February, Arsenal confirmed that Portuguese defender [[Cédric Soares]] had joined Premier League side [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] on loan until the end of the 2022–23 season.<ref name="Soares on loan"/> After the winter [[transfer window]] closed, there were twenty-four players in the first-team squad: three goalkeepers, eight defenders, six midfielders, and seven forwards. Eleven first-team players were out on loan.<ref name="first-team squad (February) AFC"/>

===February===
On 3 February, the club announced that Brazilian forward Martinelli had penned a new long-term contract.<ref name="Martinelli signed new contract AFC"/><ref name="Martinelli signed new contract TA"/> |date=4 Feb 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=5 Feb 2023 |archive-date=4 Feb 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230204232956/https://www.premierleague.com/match/75125 |url-status=live}}</ref> a team that had appointed [[Sean Dyche]] as their new manager five days previously.<ref name="EVE v ARS PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64436127 |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-Feb-04/everton-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Everton 1-0 Arsenal |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=4 Feb 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/lists/record-breaking-kane-arsenal-huge-favour-winners-losers-ratings-underwhelming-man-city/bltecd1348e36a1eba1#cs95b71998a03fb20b |title=Record-breaking Kane does |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-Feb-11/arsenal-1-1-brentford-fc-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 1-1 Brentford |last=James |first=Josh |date=11 Feb 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |archive-date=12 Feb 2023}}</ref><ref name="ARS v BRE PL VAR Independent">{{cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league-var-arsenal-brighton-b2280721.html |title=Referees
