On 15 February, Arteta's side played the postponed Premier League match at home to second-placed reigning champions Manchester City.<ref name="ARS v MCI PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75021 |title=Arsenal v Man City, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=15 Feb 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=16 Feb 2023 |archive-date=15 Feb 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230215211031/https://www.premierleague.com/match/75021 |url-status=live}}</ref> In the 24th minute, a Tomiyasu mistake allowed City's [[Kevin De Bruyne]] to score,<ref name="ARS v MCI PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/premier-league-match-report-manchester-city-emirates-stadium-bukayo-saka |title=Report: Arsenal 1-3 Manchester City |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=15 Feb 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=16 Feb 2023 |archive-date=15 Feb 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230215215348/https://www.arsenal.com/premier-league-match-report-manchester-city-emirates-stadium-bukayo-saka |url-status=live}}</ref> before a Saka penalty brought Arsenal level in the 42nd minute.<ref name="ARS v MCI PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63224218 |title=Arsenal 1-3 Manchester City: Pep Guardiola's side go top with victory at Emirates |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=15 Feb 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=16 Feb 2023 |archive-date=15 Feb 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230215230202/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63224218 |url-status=live}}</ref> Two City goals in the second half from [[Jack Grealish]] and [[Erling Haaland]] sealed a 3-1 defeat, Arsenal's first home loss in 14 league games,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/preview-arsenal-v-manchester-city |title=Preview: Arsenal v Manchester City |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=15 Feb 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=16 Feb 2023 |archive-date=15 Feb 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230215175027/https://www.arsenal.com/news/preview-arsenal-v-manchester-city |url-status=live}}</ref> and their eleventh consecutive league loss against Manchester City, their longest losing run against an opponent in their league history.<ref name="ARS v MCI PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-manchester-city/report/464745 |title=Arsenal 1-3 Man City: Erling Haaland goal caps ruthless victory as defending champions jump above Gunners at Premier League summit |last=Wright |first=Nick |date=15 Feb 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=16 Feb 2023 |archive-date=16 Feb 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230216021636/https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-manchester-city/report/464745 |url-status=live}}</ref> After the match, Arsenal swapped places with City at the top of the table on goal difference with a game in hand.<ref name="ARS v MCI PL BBC"/> The Gunners travelled to [[Villa Park]] on 18 February to play against 11th-placed Aston Villa,<ref name="AVL v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75141 |title=Aston Villa v Arsenal, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=18 Feb 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=19 Feb 2023 |archive-date=19 Feb 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230219060010/https://www.premierleague.com/match/75141 |url-status=live}}</ref> managed by former Arsenal manager [[Unai Emery]], who was facing his former club for the first time in the Premier League. In a six-goal thriller Arteta's side twice came from behind to win the match, while scoring twice in stoppage time.<ref name="AVL v ARS PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64607248 |title=Aston Villa 2-4 Arsenal: Stoppage-time goals send Gunners top of Premier League |last=De Cosemo |first=Harry |date=18 Feb 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=19 Feb 2023 |archive-date=12 Aug 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230812164042/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64607248 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="AVL v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/aston-villa-vs-arsenal/report/464865 |title=Aston Villa 2-4 Arsenal: Jorginho strike deflects in off Emi Martinez as Gunners end winless run in stoppage time |last=Bate |first=Adam |date=18 Feb 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=19 Feb 2023 |archive-date=18 Feb 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230218153524/https://www.skysports.com/football/aston-villa-vs-arsenal/report/464865 |url-status=live}}</ref> Strikes from [[Ollie Watkins]] and [[Philippe Coutinho]] were cancelled out by Saka and Zinchenko's first Premier League goal,<ref name="AVL v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-Feb-18/aston-villa-2-4-arsenal-match-report |title=Match report: Aston Villa 2-4 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=18 Feb 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=19 Feb 2023 |archive-date=18 Feb 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230218193703/https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-Feb-18/aston-villa-2-4-arsenal-match-report |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="AVL v ARS PL BBC"/><ref name="AVL v ARS PL SkySports"/> before Jorginho's long-range shot and Martinelli's counter sealed a 4-2 victory, taking Arsenal two points clear of City with a game in hand.<ref name="AVL v ARS PL SkySports"/><ref name="AVL v ARS PL AFC"/>

On 21 February, Arsenal confirmed that Egyptian midfielder Elneny, who underwent surgery to his right knee in January,<ref name="Elneny underwent surgery AFC"/><ref name="Elneny underwent surgery BBC"/> had extended his contract with the club until June 2024.<ref name="Elneny signed new contract 2 AFC"/><ref name="Elneny signed new contract 2 BBC"/> The Gunners' last match of the month was against 14th-placed Leicester City at [[King Power Stadium]] on 25 February.<ref name="LEI v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75156 |title=Leicester v Arsenal, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=25 Feb 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=26 Feb 2023 |archive-date=25 Feb 2023 respect in the week of the first anniversary of [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russia's invasion of his homeland Ukraine]].<ref name="LEI v ARS PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64686324 |title=Leicester City 0-1 Arsenal: Gabriel Martinelli goal gives Gunners win |last=Oscroft |first=Tim |date=25 Feb 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=26 Feb 2023 |archive-date=25 Feb 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230225191827/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64686324 |url-status=live}}</ref> Martinelli scored early web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/mikel-artetas-200-pl-goals |title=Mikel Arteta's 200 PL goals |last=James |first=Josh |date=25 Feb 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=26 Feb 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=26 Feb 2023 |archive-date=25 Feb 2023 the people of Ukraine.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/we-dedicate-win-ukraine |title='We dedicate the win to Ukraine' |last=James |first=Josh |date=25 Feb 2023 |website=Arsenal FC ===March===
On 1 March, the Gunners played the postponed Premier League match at home to 18th-placed Everton.<ref name="ARS v EVE PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/74971 |title=Arsenal v Everton, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=1 Mar 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=2 Mar 2023 |archive-date=1 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230301150453/https://www.premierleague.com/match/74971 |url-status=live}}</ref> Saka scored from a narrow angle five minutes before half time with his 50th goal involvement in the Premier League, before Martinelli scored in first-half stoppage time.<ref name="ARS v EVE PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-everton/report/464695 |title=Arsenal 4-0 Everton: Gabriel Martinelli scores twice as Gunners go five points clear of Man City |last=Wright |first=Nick |date=1 Mar 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=2 Mar 2023 |archive-date=2 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230302004050/https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-everton/report/464695 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="ARS v EVE PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-Mar-01/arsenal-4-0-everton-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 4-0 Everton |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=1 Mar 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=2 Mar 2023 |archive-date=1 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230301221710/https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-Mar-01/arsenal-4-0-everton-match-report |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="ARS v EVE PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62784289 |title=Arsenal 4-0 Everton: Gunners move five points clear of Man City at top of Premier League |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=1 Mar 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=2 Mar 2023 |archive-date=2 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230302002920/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62784289 |url-status=live}}</ref> Ødegaard and Martinelli scored a third and fourth in the second half to take a 4-0 victory.<ref name="ARS v EVE PL BBC"/><ref name="ARS v EVE PL SkySports"/> This was Arsenal's 100th league victory against Everton, making the Gunners the first team in English league history to register 100 wins against a specific opponent.<ref name="ARS v EVE PL SkySports"/><ref name="ARS v EVE PL AFC"/> The result moved them five points clear at the top of the Premier League.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230301-martinelli-stars-as-leaders-arsenal-crush-everton-to-go-five-points-clear |title=Martinelli stars as leaders Arsenal crush Everton to go five points clear |date=1 Mar 2023 |website=[[France 24]] |access-date=2 Mar 2023 |archive-date=2 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230302153022/https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230301-martinelli-stars-as-leaders-arsenal-crush-everton-to-go-five-points-clear |url-status=live}}</ref>

Three days later, Arteta's side played at home against 19th-placed Bournemouth.<ref name="ARS v BOU PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75161 |title=Arsenal v Bournemouth, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=4 Mar 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=5 Mar 2023 |archive-date=4 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230304203206/https://www.premierleague.com/match/75161 |url-status=live}}</ref> After Vieira replaced Xhaka in the starting lineup, this was the first time since January 1986 that Arsenal named a starting line-up without a single player to have made a competitive appearance under Wenger, who was in charge of the Gunners from 1996 to 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.90min.com/posts/arsenal-end-37-year-arsene-wenger-record-bournemouth |title=Arsenal end 37-year Arsene Wenger record in win over Bournemouth |last=Crebolder |first=Finley |date=4 Mar 2023 |website=90min |access-date=5 Mar 2023 |archive-date=4 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230304195057/https://www.90min.com/posts/arsenal-end-37-year-arsene-wenger-record-bournemouth |url-status=live}}</ref> Bournemouth took the lead after just nine seconds through [[Philip Billing]], in the second-quickest goal in Premier League history;<ref name="ARS v BOU PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64768041 |title=Arsenal 3-2 Bournemouth: Reiss Nelson gets 97th-minute winner after visitors score inside 10 seconds |last=Smith |first=Emma |date=4 Mar 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=5 Mar 2023 |archive-date=4 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230304211356/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64768041 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="ARS v BOU PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-bournemouth/report/464885 |title=Arsenal 3-2 Bournemouth: Reiss Nelson scores last-gasp winner as Gunners come from two down to beat Cherries |last=Blitz |first=Sam |date=4 Mar 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=5 Mar 2023 |archive-date=4 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230304183932/https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-bournemouth/report/464885 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="ARS v BOU PL TheTimes">{{cite web |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/arsenal-vs-bournemouth-reiss-nelsons-last-gasp-stunner-gives-arsenal-a-seismic-victory-in-title-race-x6wsc0jtl |title=Arsenal vs Bournemouth: Reiss Nelson's last-gasp stunner gives Arsenal a seismic victory in title race |last=Gheerbrant |first=James |date=4 Mar 2023 |website=The Sunday Times |access-date=5 Mar 2023 |archive-date=4 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230304214936/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/arsenal-vs-bournemouth-reiss-nelsons-last-gasp-stunner-gives-arsenal-a-seismic-victory-in-title-race-x6wsc0jtl |url-status=live}}</ref> They doubled their lead in the 57th minute through a [[Marcos Senesi]] header.<ref name="ARS v BOU PL BBC"/> Five minutes later, substitute Smith Rowe assisted Partey to reduce the deficit by one.<ref name="ARS v BOU PL SkySports"/> Nelson came on as a substitute in the 69th minute,<ref name="ARS v BOU PL TheTimes"/><ref name="ARS v BOU PL reactions BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64848020 |title=Arsenal's Reiss Nelson hits late winner: Ian Wright celebrates & pundits react |last=Smith |first=Emma |date=4 Mar 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=5 Mar 2023 |archive-date=4 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230304223343/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64848020 |url-status=live}}</ref> and assisted White's first Arsenal goal just a minute later.<ref name="ARS v BOU PL BBC"/><ref name="ARS v BOU PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-Mar-04/arsenal-3-2-bournemouth-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 3-2 Bournemouth |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=4 Mar 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=5 Mar 2023 |archive-date=4 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230304202248/https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-Mar-04/arsenal-3-2-bournemouth-match-report |url-status=live}}</ref> In the seventh minute of stoppage time, Nelson won the match with a long-range effort, sparking wild celebrations.<ref name="ARS v BOU PL TheTelegraph">{{cite web |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2023/03/04/arsenal-bournemouth-aston-villa-premier-league-live-score-goals/ |title=Super-sub Reiss Nelson completes thrilling Arsenal fightback |last=Dean |first=Sam |date=4 Mar 2023 |website=The Daily Telegraph |access-date=5 Mar 2023 |archive-date=4 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230304222721/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2023/03/04/arsenal-bournemouth-aston-villa-premier-league-live-score-goals/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="ARS v BOU PL BBC"/><ref name="ARS v BOU PL SkySports"/><ref name="ARS v BOU PL reactions BBC"/> This was the first time the Gunners had won a Premier League game in which they trailed by two or more goals since February 2012.<ref name="ARS v BOU PL SkySports"/>

On 9 March, Arsenal drew 2-2 against [[Sporting CP]] in the Europa League [[2022–23 UEFA Europa League knockout phase|last-16 first leg]] in [[Lisbon]].<ref name="SPO v ARS UEFA">{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2037610--sporting-cp-vs-arsenal/ |title=Sporting CP-Arsenal {{pipe}} UEFA Europa League 2022/23 |date=9 Mar 2023 |website=UEFA |access-date=10 Mar 2023 ARS BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64897082 |title=Sporting Lisbon 2-2 Arsenal: Gunners secure hard-earned draw in Portugal |last=Johnston |first=Neil |date=9 Mar 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=10 Mar 2023 |archive-date=10 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230310001100/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64897082 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230310024659/https://www.skysports.com/football/sporting-lisbon-vs-arsenal/report/481488 |url-status=live}}</ref> They continued their Premier League campaign on 12 March, facing seventh-placed Fulham away at [[Craven Cottage]].<ref name="FUL v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75174 |title=Fulham v Arsenal, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=12 Mar 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=13 Mar 2023 |archive-date=13 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230313032644/https://www.premierleague.com/match/75174 |url-status=live}}</ref> Gabriel Jesus was included in the Gunners' matchday squad for the first time since November 2022 following his knee injury, and came on in the second half.<ref name="FUL v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/fulham-vs-arsenal/report/464898 |title=Fulham 0-3 Arsenal: Gunners go five points clear again with slick victory as Gabriel Jesus makes comeback |last=Wright |first=Nick |date=12 Mar 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=13 Mar 2023 |archive-date=12 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230312205014/https://www.skysports.com/football/fulham-vs-arsenal/report/464898 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="FUL v ARS PL AFC"/> Goals from Gabriel Magalhães, Martinelli, and Ødegaard, all assisted by Trossard, secured a 3-0 win.<ref name="FUL v ARS PL SkySports"/><ref name="FUL v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/premier-league-match-report-fulham-gabriel-martinelli-odegaard-trossard |title=Report: Fulham 0-3 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=12 Mar 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=13 Mar 2023 |archive-date=13 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230313010348/https://www.arsenal.com/premier-league-match-report-fulham-gabriel-martinelli-odegaard-trossard |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="FUL v ARS PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64852078 |title=Fulham 0-3 Arsenal: Gunners restore five-point lead at top of table with convincing win |date=12 Mar 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=13 Mar 2023 |archive-date=12 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230312235421/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64852078 |url-status=live}}</ref> The 3–0 win was Arteta's 100th victory in all competitions as Gunners boss,<ref name="FUL v ARS PL AFC"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/arsenal-fulham-mikel-arteta-reaction-29441261 |title=Mikel Arteta's immediate response to reaching a century of Arsenal wins says it all |last=Blow |first=Tom |date=13 Mar 2023 |website=Daily Mirror |access-date=13 Mar 2023 |archive-date=13 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230313145321/https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/arsenal-fulham-mikel-arteta-reaction-29441261 |url-status=live}}</ref> making him the ninth Arsenal manager to reach the milestone,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/100-wins-under-mikel-arteta-stats |title=100 wins under Mikel Arteta: The stats |last=James |first=Josh |date=12 Mar 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=13 Mar 2023 |archive-date=13 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230313165611/https://www.arsenal.com/news/100-wins-under-mikel-arteta-stats |url-status=live}}</ref> and ensuring the Gunners became the first team in English Football League history to win five consecutive [[London derbies]] away from home without conceding a single goal.<ref>{{cite news |date=12 Mar 2023 |title=Soccer-Leaders Arsenal crush Fulham, Man United held, Newcastle win |url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/soccer-leaders-arsenal-crush-fulham-man-united-held-newcastle-win-2023-03-12/ |url-status=live |work=Reuters |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230313005822/https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/soccer-leaders-arsenal-crush-fulham-man-united-held-newcastle-win-2023-03-12/ |archive-date=13 Mar 2023 |access-date=13 Mar 2023}}</ref> Arsenal's fine form during the season was recognised at the 2023 London Football Awards, which took place on 13 March. Ødegaard picked up the Premier League Player of the Year award, Saka won the Men's Young Player of the Year award, Ramsdale received the Goalkeeper of the Year award, and Arteta was named Manager of the Year.<ref name="London Football Awards"/><ref name="London Football Awards 90min"/>

The Gunners hosted Sporting CP in the second leg on 16 March.<ref name="ARS v SPO UEFA">{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2037618--arsenal-vs-sporting-cp/ |title=Arsenal-Sporting CP {{pipe}} UEFA Europa League 2022/23 |date=16 Mar 2023 |website=UEFA |access-date=17 Mar 2023 |archive-date=15 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230315133738/https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2037618--arsenal-vs-sporting-cp/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Xhaka put Arsenal ahead, before [[Pedro Gonçalves]] levelled with a 46-yard chip.<ref name="ARS v SPO AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/europa-league-match-report-sporting-cp-emirates-stadium |title=Report: Arsenal 1-1 Sporting CP (3-5 penalties) |last=James |first=Josh |date=16 Mar 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=17 Mar 2023 |archive-date=17 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230317161222/https://www.arsenal.com/europa-league-match-report-sporting-cp-emirates-stadium |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="ARS v SPO SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-sporting-lisbon/report/481489 |title=Arsenal 1-1 Sporting (Agg 3-3; 3-5 on pens): Gabriel Martinelli misses from spot as Gunners crash out of Europa League |last=Smith |first=Peter |date=17 Mar 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=17 Mar 2023}}</ref><ref name="ARS v SPO BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64971711 |title=Arsenal 1-1 Sporting Lisbon: Arsenal knocked out of Europa League in penalty shootout defeat |last=Sanders |first=Emma |date=16 Mar 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=17 Mar 2023 |archive-date=17 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230317000800/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64971711 |url-status=live}}</ref> Arsenal had several chances to score in extra-time, but despite [[Manuel Ugarte (footballer)|Manuel Ugarte]] receiving a second yellow card, the Portuguese side held out to force the game to [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]], which they won 5-3.<ref name="ARS v SPO BBC"/><ref name="ARS v SPO SkySports"/> Ahead of the last [[FIFA International Match Calendar|international break]] of the season, the Gunners played at home on 19 March against 12th-placed Crystal Palace,<ref name="ARS v CRY PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75181 |title=Arsenal v Crystal Palace, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=19 Mar 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=20 Mar 2023 |archive-date=19 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319224012/https://www.premierleague.com/match/75181 |url-status=live}}</ref> who had sacked manager and former Arsenal captain Patrick Vieira two days previously.<ref name="ARS v CRY PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64929886 |title=Arsenal 4-1 Crystal Palace: Gunners go eight points clear at top of Premier League |last=Emons |first=Michael |date=19 Mar 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=20 Mar 2023 |archive-date=20 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230320000720/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64929886 |url-status=live}}</ref> Martinelli scored his sixth goal in six Premier League games in the 28th minute with a left-footed strike, before Saka's brace and Xhaka's strike secured a 4-1 win.<ref name="ARS v CRY PL BBC"/><ref name="ARS v CRY PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-Mar-19/arsenal-4-1-crystal-palace-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 4-1 Crystal Palace |last=James |first=Josh |date=19 Mar 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=20 Mar 2023 |archive-date=19 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319212422/https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-Mar-19/arsenal-4-1-crystal-palace-match-report |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="ARS v CRY PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-crystal-palace/report/464905 |title=Arsenal 4-1 Crystal Palace: Bukayo Saka scores twice as Gunners extend lead to eight points over Man City |last=Richardson |first=David |date=19 Mar 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=20 Mar 2023 |archive-date=20 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230320143118/https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-crystal-palace/report/464905 |url-status=live}}</ref> The victory extended the Gunners' winning streak to six in the league, and gave them an eight-point advantage over Manchester City with their opponents having a game in hand.<ref name="ARS v CRY PL BBC"/> With 10 league games to go, the Gunners had notched up 69 points to reach their same points tally as the previous season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/match-reports/arsenal-crystal-palace-saka-martinelli-29497414 |title=Bukayo Saka dominates as Arsenal take eight-point lead in title race – 5 talking points |last=Keith |first=Felix |date=19 Mar 2023 |website=Daily Mirror |access-date=20 Mar 2023}}</ref> The Gunners became the first side in English Football League history to win nine London derbies in a single league campaign.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/12838007/arsenal-4-1-crystal-palace-mikel-arteta-calls-on-his-players-to-give-a-little-bit-more-to-withstand-man-city |title=Arsenal 4-1 Crystal Palace: Mikel Arteta calls on his players to 'give a little bit more' to withstand Man City |last=Grounds |first=Ben |date=19 Mar 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=20 Mar 2023 |archive-date=20 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230320003006/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/12838007/arsenal-4-1-crystal-palace-mikel-arteta-calls-on-his-players-to-give-a-little-bit-more-to-withstand-man-city |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 21 March, Arsenal confirmed that defender Tomiyasu, who had suffered a significant injury in the match against Sporting five days ago, had undergone surgery to his right knee. Tomiyasu would miss the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/takehiro-tomiyasu-injury-medical-update |title=Medical update: Takehiro Tomiyasu |date=21 Mar 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=22 Mar 2023}}</ref><ref name="Tomiyasu underwent surgery BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65032396 |title=Takehiro Tomiyasu: Arsenal full-back ruled out for rest of season with knee injury |date=21 Mar 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=22 Mar 2023 |archive-date=22 Mar 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230322015411/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65032396 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Arteta picked up his fourth Premier League Manager of the Month award of the season,<ref name="Arteta named March's PL MOTM"/> becoming the third manager in Premier League history to do so in a single campaign, after Guardiola in 2017–18 and Klopp in 2019–20.<ref name="Arteta won four PL MOTM awards in a season OptaJoe"/> Saka won the Premier League Player of the Month award for the first time in his career.<ref name="Saka named March's PL POTM"/> Ramsdale's vital save to deny Bournemouth's Dango Ouattara won the Premier League Save of the Month award, making him the first Arsenal goalkeeper to claim the award.<ref name="Ramsdale claimed March's PL SOTM"/>

===April===
After the international break, Arsenal faced 14th-placed Leeds United at home on 1 April.<ref name="ARS v LEE PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75191 |title=Arsenal v Leeds, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=1 Apr 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=2 Apr 2023}}</ref> Jesus opened the scoring with a penalty in the 12th minute,<ref name="ARS v LEE PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-leeds-united/report/464915 |title=Arsenal 4-1 Leeds: Gabriel Jesus scores twice as Gunners restore eight-point lead at top of Premier League |last=Yew |first=Oliver |date=1 Apr 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=2 Apr 2023}}</ref> before White doubled the lead early in the second half.<ref name="ARS v LEE PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-Apr-01/arsenal-4-1-leeds-united-fc-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 4-1 Leeds United |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=1 Apr 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=2 Apr 2023}}</ref> Gabriel Jesus netted his second eight minutes later,<ref name="ARS v LEE PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65073189 |title=Arsenal 4-1 Leeds United: Gabriel Jesus scores twice as Gunners restore eight-point lead |last=Howarth |first=Matthew |date=1 Apr 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=2 Apr 2023}}</ref> and although [[Rasmus Kristensen]] pulled one back,<ref name="ARS v LEE PL SkySports"/> Xhaka restored the Gunners' three-goal lead on 84 minutes.<ref name="ARS v LEE PL AFC"/> The victory was Arteta's 100th in all competitions as Arsenal manager.<ref name="ARS v LEE PL BBC"/> The Gunners headed to [[Anfield]] to take on eighth-placed Liverpool on 9 April.<ref name="LIV v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75206 |title=Liverpool v Arsenal, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=9 Apr 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=10 Apr 2023}}</ref> Martinelli opened with his 25th Premier League goal, before assisting Jesus in the 28th minute.<ref name="LIV v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/report-liverpool-2-2-arsenal |title=Report: Liverpool 2-2 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=9 Apr 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=10 Apr 2023}}</ref><ref name="LIV v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/liverpool-vs-arsenal/report/464930 |title=Liverpool 2-2 Arsenal: Late Roberto Firmino leveller blows title race wide open |last=Wilkinson |first=Jack |date=9 Apr 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=10 Apr 2023}}</ref> The hosts however pulled one back through [[Mohamed Salah]] on 42 minutes, who missed a penalty seven minutes into the second half, before Firmino scored a late equaliser in the 87th minute after sustained Liverpool pressure.<ref name="LIV v ARS PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65152635 |title=Liverpool 2-2 Arsenal: Roberto Firmino scores late equaliser to hurt Gunners' title bid |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=9 Apr 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=10 Apr 2023}}</ref><ref name="LIV v ARS PL SkySports"/><ref name="LIV v ARS PL AFC"/> In stoppage time, Ramsdale produced a flying fingertip save to deny Salah's deflected curling shot, then kept out [[Ibrahima Konaté]]'s effort from point-blank range.<ref name="LIV v ARS PL BBC"/> The Gunners' seven-game winning run in the Premier League came to an end.<ref name="LIV v ARS PL SkySports"/>

On 16 April, Arteta's side faced 14th-placed West Ham United at [[London Stadium]].<ref name="WHU v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75219 |title=West Ham v Arsenal, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=16 Apr 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=17 Apr 2023}}</ref> Gabriel Jesus scored his fourth goal in three matches in the seventh minute,<ref name="WHU v ARS PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65223931 |title=West Ham 2-2 Arsenal: Bukayo Saka misses penalty as Gunners let slip two-goal lead |last=Emons |first=Michael |date=16 Apr 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=17 Apr 2023}}</ref> before Ødegaard volleyed in a second three minutes later.<ref name="WHU v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-Apr-16/west-ham-united-2-2-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: West Ham 2-2 Arsenal |last=Small |first=Aidan |date=16 Apr 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=17 Apr 2023}}</ref> However, Benrahma and Bowen pulled two goals back, with Saka also missing a penalty, to ensure that the Gunners had let a two-goal lead slip in consecutive league games.<ref name="WHU v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/west-ham-united-vs-arsenal/report/464943 |title=West Ham 2-2 Arsenal: Mikel Arteta's side throw away another two-goal advantage on the road in title race with Man City |last=Blitz |first=Sam |date=16 Apr 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=17 Apr 2023}}</ref><ref name="WHU v ARS PL BBC"/><ref name="WHU v ARS PL AFC"/> Five days later, the Gunners played at home against 20th-placed Southampton.<ref name="ARS v SOU PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75221 |title=Arsenal v Southampton, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=21 Apr 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=22 Apr 2023}}</ref> The away team took a surprise lead through [[Theo Walcott]] after 28 seconds,<ref name="ARS v SOU PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-southampton/report/464945 |title=Arsenal 3-3 Southampton: Gunners stage dramatic comeback but more ground lost in Premier League title race |last=Wilkinson |first=Jack |date=21 Apr 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=22 Apr 2023}}</ref><ref name="ARS v SOU PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65271717 |title=Arsenal 3-3 Southampton: Premier League leaders fight back to draw third game in a row |last=Smith |first=Emma |date=21 Apr 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=22 Apr 2023}}</ref> and he doubled their lead fourteen minutes later.<ref name="ARS v SOU PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-Apr-21/arsenal-3-3-southampton-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 3-3 Southampton |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=21 Apr 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=22 Apr 2023}}</ref> Martinelli pulled one back with his 15th league goal,<ref name="ARS v SOU PL BBC 2">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65356177 |title=Arsenal 'have to beat Man City' after another stumble in Premier League title race |last=Smith |first=Emma |date=21 Apr 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=22 Apr 2023}}</ref> before [[Duje Ćaleta-Car]] restored Southampton's two-goal cushion on 66 minutes.<ref name="ARS v SOU PL SkySports"/> Two late goals from Ødegaard and Saka earned Arsenal a 3-3 draw,<ref name="ARS v SOU PL AFC"/><ref name="ARS v SOU PL SkySports"/> leaving the Gunners five points ahead of Manchester City, who had two games in hand.<ref name="ARS v SOU PL BBC"/>

The top two teams faced each other at the Etihad Stadium on 26 April.<ref name="MCI v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75239 |title=Man City v Arsenal, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=26 Apr 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=27 Apr 2023}}</ref> Saliba remained out with a back injury,<ref name="MCI v ARS PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65319949 |title=Manchester City 4-1 Arsenal: Kevin de Bruyne scores two and makes one in dominant display |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=26 Apr 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=27 Apr 2023}}</ref><ref name="MCI v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/manchester-city-vs-arsenal/report/464963 |title=Man City 4-1 Arsenal: Kevin De Bruyne scores two as Pep Guardiola's treble-chasers take charge of title race |last=Bate |first=Adam |date=26 Apr 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=27 Apr 2023}}</ref> and captain Ødegaard made his 100th appearance for the team in all competitions.<ref name="Line-up MCI v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/team-news-xhaka-back-city-clash |title=Team news: Xhaka back for City clash |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=26 Apr 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=27 Apr 2023}}</ref> [[Kevin De Bruyne]] opened the scoring for City seven minutes in,<ref name="MCI v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-Apr-26/manchester-city-4-1-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Manchester City 4-1 Arsenal |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=26 Apr 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=27 Apr 2023}}</ref> before [[John Stones]] doubled their lead in first-half stoppage time.<ref name="MCI v ARS PL BBC"/> De Bruyne scored his second nine minutes into the second half, and although Arsenal pulled one back through Holding in the 86th minute, Haaland netted in second-half stoppage time, sealing a 4–1 win for the hosts, and ending Arsenal's ten-game unbeaten run in the Premier League.<ref name="MCI v ARS PL AFC"/><ref name="MCI v ARS PL SkySports"/> This was Arsenal's twelfth consecutive Premier League loss against City, with an aggregate score of 5–33.<ref name="MCI v ARS PL SkySports"/> After the match, their lead at the top of the league was cut to two points over Guardiola's side who had two games in hand and a superior goal difference.<ref name="MCI v ARS PL BBC"/> Despite the loss, Arteta's side mathematically qualified for next season's [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] after a six-year absence.<ref name="MCI v ARS PL SkySports"/>

Ramsdale's vital save to deny Liverpool's Salah won the Premier League Save of the Month award, making him the first Arsenal goalkeeper to receive the award back to back.<ref name="Ramsdale claimed April's PL SOTM"/>

===May===
The club started May with a 3–1 win over 12th-placed Chelsea at home on 2 May.<ref name="ARS v CHE PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75241 |title=Arsenal v Chelsea, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=2 May 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=3 May 2023}}</ref> The Gunners dominated the first half, with Ødegaard netting twice and Gabriel Jesus once.<ref name="ARS v CHE PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65382202 |title=Arsenal 3-1 Chelsea: Martin Odegaard double helps Arsenal back to top of Premier League |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=2 May 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=3 May 2023}}</ref><ref name="ARS v CHE PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-May-02/arsenal-3-1-chelsea-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 3-1 Chelsea |last=James |first=Josh |date=2 May 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=3 May 2023}}</ref> This marked the second time the club had four players (Saka, Martinelli, Ødegaard and Gabriel Jesus) reach double figures for goals in a Premier League season, after [[2012–13 Arsenal F.C. season|2012–13]].<ref name="Talking points ARS v CHE PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/5-talking-points-following-our-win-against-chelsea |title=5 talking points following our win against Chelsea |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=2 May 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=3 May 2023}}</ref> The result secured the Gunners' fourth Premier League double over Chelsea<ref name="ARS v CHE PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-chelsea/report/464965 |title=Arsenal 3-1 Chelsea: Martin Odegaard scores twice as Gunners keep title bid alive and go back above Man City |last=Wright |first=Nick |date=2 May 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=3 May 2023}}</ref> and ensured it was the first time since February 2004 that Arsenal had won three consecutive Premier League games against the Blues.<ref name="Talking points ARS v CHE PL AFC"/> After the game, the club condemned the behaviour of a man who shone a [[laser]] in the face of Chelsea player [[Mykhailo Mudryk]]. The Metropolitan Police confirmed a 21-year-old man was arrested after the incident.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65469443 |title=Mykhailo Mudryk: Man, 21, arrested for shining laser at Chelsea winger during Arsenal defeat |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=3 May 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=3 May 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4483992/2023/05/03/mykhailo-mudryk-laser-arsenal-chelsea/ |title=Fan arrested after Mykhailo Mudryk laser incident during Arsenal win over Chelsea |last=Rampling |first=Ali |date=3 May 2023 |website=The Athletic |access-date=3 May 2023}}</ref> The Gunners faced third-placed Newcastle United at [[St James' Park]] on 7 May.<ref name="NEW v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75256 |title=Newcastle v Arsenal, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=7 May 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=8 May 2023}}</ref><ref name="NEW v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/newcastle-united-vs-arsenal/report/464980 |title=Newcastle 0-2 Arsenal: Gunners show their mettle in vital St James' Park win |date=7 May 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=8 May 2023}}</ref> Arsenal secured a 2-0 victory, courtesy of an early Ødegaard strike and a [[Fabian Schär]] own goal.<ref name="NEW v ARS PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65439739 |title=Newcastle United 0-2 Arsenal: Gunners keep Premier League title hopes alive with win |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=7 May 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=8 May 2023}}</ref> The Gunners had 81 points from 35 Premier League matches this campaign, a point behind leaders Manchester City who still had a game in hand.<ref name="NEW v ARS PL SkySports"/><ref name="NEW v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-May-07/newcastle-united-0-2-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Newcastle United 0-2 Arsenal |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=7 May 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=8 May 2023}}</ref>

Arsenal faced to seventh-placed Brighton & Hove Albion at home on 14 May.<ref name="ARS v BHA PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75261 |title=Arsenal v Brighton, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=14 May 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=15 May 2023}}</ref> Second-half goals from [[Julio Enciso (footballer, born 2004)|Julio Enciso]], [[Deniz Undav]], and [[Pervis Estupiñán]] sealed a 3-0 win for the visitors.<ref name="ARS v BHA PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-May-14/arsenal-0-3-brighton-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 0-3 Brighton & Hove Albion |last=James |first=Josh |date=14 May 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=15 May 2023}}</ref><ref name="ARS v BHA PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-brighton-and-hove-albion/report/464985 |title=Arsenal 0-3 Brighton: Gunners' Premier League title hopes left in tatters by sensational Seagulls |last=Shread |first=Joe |date=14 May 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=15 May 2023}}</ref> Four days later, the club announced that English goalkeeper Ramsdale had signed a new long-term contract.<ref name="Ramsdale signed new contract AFC"/><ref name="Ramsdale signed new contract TA"/>

In their final away game of the season, Arsenal faced 16th-placed Nottingham Forest at the [[City Ground]] on 20 May.<ref name="NFO v ARS PL">{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75277 |title=Nott'm Forest v Arsenal, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=20 May 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=21 May 2023}}</ref> Arsenal lost 1-0, courtesy of an early goal from [[Taiwo Awoniyi]]; the result sealed Forest's place in the top flight, and allowed Manchester City to clinch the Premier League title with three games still to play.<ref name="NFO v ARS PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/nottingham-forest-vs-arsenal/report/465001 |title=Nottingham Forest 1-0 Arsenal: Taiwo Awoniyi's early goal clinches survival as Man City confirmed Premier League champions |last=Wright |first=Nick |date=20 May 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=21 May 2023}}</ref> In contrast to the first half of the season, when Arteta's side only dropped 7 points in 19 games (16 wins, 2 draws and 1 loss), they had collected just 9 points from their past 8 matches (2 wins, 3 draws and 3 losses).<ref name="NFO v ARS PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65579920 |title=Nottingham Forest 1-0 Arsenal: Hosts secure Premier League safety to hand title to Manchester City |last=Stone |first=Simon |date=20 May 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=21 May 2023}}</ref><ref name="NFO v ARS PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-May-20/nottingham-forest-1-0-arsenal-match-report |title=Report: Nottingham Forest 1-0 Arsenal |last=James |first=Josh |date=20 May 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=21 May 2023}}</ref> The Gunners were eight points clear of Guardiola's side earlier this season and had led the league for a long time, but ultimately their challenge collapsed.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12885703/jamie-carragher-says-arsenal-blew-it-and-need-more-depth-to-compete-with-man-city-as-mikel-arteta-apologises-for-falling-short-in-title-race |title=Jamie Carragher says Arsenal 'blew it' and need more depth to compete with Man City as Mikel Arteta apologises for falling short in title race |last=Carragher |first=Jamie |author-link=Jamie Carragher |date=20 May 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=21 May 2023}}</ref> In fact, Arsenal topped the Premier League table for 248 days over the course of this campaign, the most without finishing first in English top-flight history.<ref name="MCI won PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65613744 |title=Manchester City win Premier League for third successive season after Arsenal lose |date=20 May 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=21 May 2023}}</ref>

The club confirmed on 23 May that English forward Saka had signed a new long-term contract.<ref name="Saka signed new contract AFC"/><ref name="Saka signed new contract BBC"/> The Gunners' final game of the season was at home against 13th-placed Wolverhampton Wanderers.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/75281 |title=Arsenal v Wolves, 2022/23 {{pipe}} Premier League |date=28 May 2023 |website=Premier League |access-date=29 May 2023}}</ref> Two goals from Xhaka—his first brace for Arsenal in his 297th appearance—were followed by strikes from Saka, Jesus, and Kiwior's first Arsenal goal.<ref name="ARS v WOL PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2023-May-28/arsenal-5-0-wolves-match-report |title=Report: Arsenal 5-0 Wolverhampton Wanderers |last=Rogers |first=Jonathon |date=28 May 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=29 May 2023}}</ref><ref name="ARS v WOL PL BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65661810 |title=Arsenal 5-0 Wolverhampton Wanderers: Hosts record thumping win |last=Sutcliffe |first=Steve |date=28 May 2023 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=29 May 2023}}</ref><ref name="Talking points ARS v WOL PL AFC">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/five-talking-points-wolves-win |title=Five talking points from our Wolves win |last=James |first=Josh |date=28 May 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=29 May 2023}}</ref><ref name="ARS v WOL PL SkySports">{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-wolverhampton-wanderers/report/465005 |title=Arsenal 5-0 Wolves: Granit Xhaka scores twice on Emirates Stadium farewell as Gunners finish on a high |last=Wright |first=Nick |date=28 May 2023 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=29 May 2023}}</ref> The 5–0 win meant that Arteta's side finished the Premier League campaign in second place, five points behind champions Manchester City.<ref name="ARS v WOL PL AFC"/><ref name="ARS v WOL PL BBC"/>

Arsenal's performances this campaign led to several season award nominations. Arteta was nominated for [[Premier League Manager of the Season]];<ref name="Arteta nominated PL MOTS"/> Ødegaard and Saka were shortlisted for [[Premier League Player of the Season]];<ref name="Odegaard & Saka nominated PL POTS"/> Martinelli, Ødegaard and Saka were included on the shortlist for the [[Premier League Young Player of the Season]] award;<ref name="Martinelli, Odegaard & Saka nominated PL YPOTS"/> Ramsdale's vital stop to deny Bournemouth's Dango Ouattara on 4 March and his flying fingertip save to stop Liverpool's Salah from scoring a deflected curling shot on 9 April were nominated for the [[Premier League Save of the Season]] award;<ref name="Ramsdale nominated PL SOTS"/> while Nelson won the [[Premier League Game Changer of the Season]] award, as his performance transformed the match against Bournemouth on 4 March.<ref name="Nelson won PL GCOTS"/> Arteta was also in contention for the [[League Managers Association]] (LMA) [[LMA Manager of the Year|Manager of the Year]] award.<ref name="LMA MOTY"/> Ødegaard and Saka were nominated for [[Professional Footballers' Association]] (PFA) [[PFA Players' Player of the Year|Players' Player of the Year]];<ref name="PFA Player' POTY nominees"/> Martinelli and Saka were included on the shortlist for the [[PFA Young Player of the Year]] award,<ref name="PFA YPOTY nominees"/> which was won by Saka;<ref name="Saka won PFA YPOTY"/> Ødegaard, Ramsdale, Saka and Saliba were selected for the [[PFA Team of the Year (2020s)|PFA Premier League Team of the Year]];<ref name="PFA TOTY"/> Ødegaard and Saka were also in contention for the [[PFA Fans' Player of the Year|PFA Premier League Fans' Player of the Year]] award.<ref name="PFA Fans' POTY nominees 90min"/> Saka and Ødegaard finished second and third respectively in the [[Football Writers' Association]] (FWA) [[FWA Footballer of the Year|Footballer of the Year]] award.<ref name="FWA FOTY"/> Ødegaard and Saka were nominated for the [[2023 Ballon d'Or]],<ref name="Ballon d'Or"/> while Ramsdale was shortlisted for the [[2023 Ballon d'Or#Yashin Trophy|2023 Yashin Trophy]].<ref name="Yashin Trophy"/> Ødegaard was voted as Arsenal's [[Arsenal Player of the Season|Player of the Season]],<ref name="Ødegaard voted as AFC POTS"/> and Nelson's last-gasp strike against Bournemouth was voted as the club's Goal of the Season.<ref name="Nelson's strike voted as AFC GOTS"/>

===June===
Due to Premier League champions Manchester City winning the [[2023 FA Cup final]] on 3 June, Arsenal, the league runners-up, would play against them in the [[2023 FA Community Shield]] in August.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/arsenal-man-city-community-shield-30148472 |title=When is Community Shield 2023? Arsenal set to face Man City in season curtain raiser |last=Meade |first=Samuel |date=3 Jun 2023 |website=Daily Mirror |access-date=3 Jun 2023}}</ref>

The Gunners' [[UEFA coefficient#Men's club coefficient|UEFA club coefficient]] was 76.000 points at the end of this campaign.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/nationalassociations/uefarankings/club/#/yr/2023 |title=Club coefficients {{pipe}} UEFA Coefficients |date=7 Jun 2023 |website=UEFA |access-date=12 Jun 2023 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612083123/https://www.uefa.com/nationalassociations/uefarankings/club/#/yr/2023 |archive-date=12 Jun 2023}}</ref> They would be in Pot 2 for the [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|2023–24 Champions League]] [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League group stage|group stage]] draw.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/arsenal-champions-league-group-draw-opponents-pot-b1084345.html |title=Arsenal's potential Champions League opponents revealed with pot confirmed for 2023/24 draw |last=Mayo |first=Marc |date=29 May 2023 |website=Evening Standard |access-date=29 May 2023}}</ref>

===Kit information===
This is Adidas's fourth year supplying Arsenal kit, having taken over from [[Puma (brand)|Puma]] at the beginning of the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/adidas-and-arsenal-launch-new-home-kit |title=adidas and Arsenal launch new home kit |date=1 Jul 2019 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=23 May 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.adidas.com/football/adidas-and-arsenal-launch-new-partnership-with-2019-20-home-kit/s/a792ee1b-7f39-4f66-a095-a689e151ec5b |title=adidas and Arsenal launch new partnership with 2019/20 home kit |date=1 Jul 2019 |website=Adidas |access-date=23 May 2022}}</ref> On 30 September 2022, Arsenal announced the extension of the partnership with Adidas until 2030.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/adidas-partnership-extended-2030 |title=adidas partnership extended to 2030 |date=30 Sep 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=30 Sep 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.football.london/arsenal-fc/news/arsenal-financial-boost-adidas-deal-25188597 |title=Arsenal handed huge £120m financial boost as details of new £600m Adidas deal emerges |last=Thrower |first=Luke |date=5 Oct 2022 |website=football.london |access-date=6 Oct 2022}}</ref>

*'''Home:''' The club confirmed on 19 May 2022 that their new home kit for the 2022–23 season would debut in the final home game of the 2021–22 season. The home kit uses Arsenal's traditional colours of red and white. The shirt has a red body and white sleeves, and is complemented by white shorts and red socks. The new feature added to the home kit is a lightning bolt pattern appearing on the collar and socks.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/feelslikehome |title=Introducing our new home kit for 2022/23! |date=19 May 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=23 May 2022}}</ref>
*'''Away:''' On 18 July 2022, the Gunners released their new away kit. The all-black shirt combines a bronze cannon badge and metallic trims with an all-over AFC graphic, and is partnered with black shorts and socks.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/introducing-our-new-away-kit-202223-0 |title=Introducing our new away kit for 2022/23 |date=18 Jul 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=19 Jul 2022}}</ref> White shorts and grey socks were used in some away games when there was a colour clash with the home team's kit. It was reported that Arsenal sold [[Pound sterling|£]]1&nbsp;million of the new away kit on launch day, a new club's record for first-day kit sales.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sportbible.com/afcstuff/arsenal-news-away-kit-sales-20220719 |title=Arsenal Break Kit Sale Records With Classy New Away Shirt |last=Lennard |first=Jake |date=19 Jul 2022 |website=[[SPORTbible]] |access-date=20 Jul 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet |author=FourFourTwo |author-link=FourFourTwo |user=FourFourTwo |number=1550431747015409665 |date=22 Jul 2022 |title=Arsenal set a new record for first-day kit sales: their 2022/23 away shirt brought in £1 million in the first 24 hours 😲 |access-date=23 Jul 2022}}</ref>
*'''Third:''' The new third kit was revealed on 29 July 2022, one day before the [[2022 Emirates Cup]] match. It is the first pink outfield shirt in Arsenal's history. The shirt features an all-over ermine print, and is combined with navy shorts and pink socks.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/introducing-our-new-202223-adidas-third-kit |title=Introducing our new 2022/23 adidas third kit |date=29 Jul 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=30 Jul 2022}}</ref>
*'''No More Red:''' On 6 January 2023, Arsenal announced that they were going to extend their "No More Red" campaign for a second season; an initiative that aims to combat knife crime in the [[London|capital]]. The same commemorative kit from the previous season was used this season, with typical white features set upon a slightly off-white kit.<ref name="No More Red kit">{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/adidas-and-arsenal-expand-no-more-red-campaign |title=adidas and Arsenal expand No More Red campaign |date=6 Jan 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=7 Jan 2023}}</ref>
*'''Goalkeeper:''' The new goalkeeper kits are based on Adidas's goalkeeper template for the season.

==Pre-season and friendlies==
<!-- Update source: https://www.arsenal.com/results -->
On 19 April 2022, Arsenal announced that they would travel to the United States in July to compete in the [[Florida Cup (soccer)|FC Series]] as part of their preparations during pre-season with matches against [[Orlando City SC|Orlando City]] and [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/florida-cup-series-arsenal-chelsea-orlando-city-pre-season-united-states |title=Arsenal to head to the US to compete in FC Series |date=19 Apr 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=21 Apr 2022}}</ref> On 10 May, a further US tour friendly was confirmed against [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] in The Charm City Match in July.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/pre-season-friendly-US-tour-everton-baltimore-charm-city-match |title=Arsenal to take on Everton in Baltimore |date=10 May 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=11 May 2022}}</ref> On 18 May, La Liga side [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] revealed their participation in the [[2022 Emirates Cup]] in late July.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sevillafc.es/en/actual/news/announcement-emirates-cup-2022 |title=A trip to London to play in the Emirates Cup |date=18 May 2022 |website=Sevilla FC |access-date=19 May 2022}}</ref> On 6 June, Arsenal announced that they would travel to Germany to face [[1. FC Nürnberg]] as part of a pre-season training camp at the Adidas headquarters in July, before heading to the US.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/were-heading-germany-face-1-fc-nurnberg |title=We're heading to Germany to face 1. FC Nürnberg |date=6 Jun 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=7 Jun 2022}}</ref>

In order to prepare for the resumption of the Premier League following the mid-season World Cup break, Arsenal announced that they were going to partake in a warm-weather training camp in Dubai, United Arab Emirates in early December. This involved participating in the Dubai Super Cup against [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] and [[AC Milan|Milan]] on 8 and 13 December respectively.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-set-dubai-super-cup-during-world-cup |title=Arsenal set for Dubai Super Cup during World Cup |date=15 Nov 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=2 Dec 2022}}</ref> Arsenal then announced a final friendly against Serie A side [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] to be played on 17 December.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/arsenal-host-juventus-emirates-stadium |title=Arsenal to host Juventus at Emirates Stadium |date=24 Nov 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=2 Dec 2022}}</ref>

===Premier League===
{{main|2022–23 Premier League}}

Arsenal won 26 league games this season, equalling their highest-ever tally in the Premier League, which were also achieved in 2001–02 and 2003–04. They ended the campaign on 84 points, the third-highest total in their history.<ref name="season statistics AFC"/><ref name="ARS v WOL PL AFC"/> This was the first time the Gunners finished in the top four since the 2015–16 season.<ref name="MCI v ARS PL SkySports"/>

===FA Cup===
{{main|2022–23 FA Cup}}

As a Premier League side, Arsenal entered the FA Cup in the third round. They were drawn away to [[EFL League One|League One]] side [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/gunners-face-oxford-fa-cup-third-round |title=Gunners to face Oxford in FA Cup third round |date=28 Nov 2022 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=29 Nov 2022}}</ref> In the fourth round, they were drawn away to fellow Premier League side [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/fa-cup-fourth-round-draw-made |title=FA Cup fourth round draw made |date=8 Jan 2023 |website=Arsenal FC |access-date=10 Jan 2023}}</ref>

====Knockout phase====
{{main|2022–23 UEFA Europa League knockout phase}}

=====Round of 16=====
As a result of finishing top of the group, Arsenal advanced directly to the round of 16. The draw was held on 24 February 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/draws/2023/2001682/ |title=UEFA Europa League round of 16 draw |website=UEFA |date=24 Feb 2023 |access-date=24 Feb 2023}}</ref> As a seeded team, Arsenal played the second leg at home.

===Appearances===
Twenty-eight players made appearances for Arsenal's first team during the season; six of them (Gabriel Magalhães, Martinelli, Ødegaard, Saka, White and Xhaka) each played at least 45 of the total 49 matches.<ref name="season statistics AFC"/>

This was the first time since [[1990–91 Arsenal F.C. season|1990–91]] that the Gunners had four players (Gabriel Magalhães, Ramsdale, Saka and White) feature in every top-flight game.<ref name="Talking points ARS v WOL PL AFC"/> Ramsdale became the first Arsenal player to be on the pitch for every minute of the league season since goalkeeper [[Wojciech Szczęsny]] in [[2011–12 Arsenal F.C. season|2011–12]].<ref name="season statistics AFC"/>

The Gunners were the most settled side of the Premier League season, as Arteta made the fewest changes to his starting XI between matches (just 38 across the whole campaign).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4559451/2023/05/29/the-alternative-premier-league-awards/ |title=The alternative Premier League awards: Biggest overperformer? Fastest shot? Sweepiest goalkeeper? |last=Carey |first=Mark |date=29 May 2023 |website=The Athletic |access-date=29 May 2023}}</ref><ref name="season statistics AFC"/>

Arsenal had the second-youngest average starting line-up in the 2022–23 Premier League, at 25 years and 52 days – 11 days older than Relegated Southampton, and 2 years and 201 days younger than champions Manchester City.<ref name="youngest teams BBC"/><ref name="season statistics AFC"/>

===Goals===
Arsenal scored 103 goals in all competitions this season, which was the first time they reached three figures since [[2018–19 Arsenal F.C. season|2018–19]]. They scored club-record 88 goals in the Premier League – the most they got in any top-flight campaign since [[1963–64 Arsenal F.C. season|1963–64]].<ref name="Talking points ARS v WOL PL AFC"/>

Nineteen players scored for Arsenal's first team during the season, sixteen of them netted in the Premier League. This was the first time since [[1970–71 Arsenal F.C. season|1970–71]] that the Gunners had two players (Martinelli and Ødegaard) score at least 15 league goals.<ref name="season statistics AFC"/>

====Premier League Manager of the Month====
The winner of the [[Premier League Manager of the Month|award]] was chosen by a combination of an online public vote and a panel of experts.

Arteta picked up four Premier League's Manager of the Month awards in the 2022–23 season, becoming the third manager in Premier League history to do so in a single campaign.<ref name="Arteta won four PL MOTM awards in a season OptaJoe">{{cite tweet |author=OptaJoe |user=OptaJoe |number=1641760646390841344 |date=31 Mar 2023 |title=4 – Mikel Arteta has become only the third manager in history to win four @premierleague Manager of the Month awards in a single season, after Pep Guardiola in 2017-18 (4) and Jürgen Klopp in 2019-20 (5). Fantastic. |access-date=31 Mar 2023}}</ref> As manager of Arsenal, he had six awards in total up until that point, the [[Premier League Manager of the Month#Multiple winners|joint-9th]] highest awards a single manager had received since its inception in August 1993.<ref name="Arteta named March's PL MOTM"/>

====Premier League Player of the Month====
The winner of the [[Premier League Player of the Month|award]] was chosen by a combination of an online public vote, a panel of experts, and the captain of each Premier League club.

Ødegaard won the Premier League's Player of the Month award after league-high six goal involvements (three goals and three assists) across November and December 2022.<ref name="Ødegaard named November/December's PL POTM"/> Saka won the Premier League's Player of the Month award (for the first time in his career) in March 2023, after joint-league-high five goal involvements (three goals and two assists).<ref name="Saka named March's PL POTM"/>

====Premier League Save of the Month====
The winner of the [[Premier League Save of the Month|award]] was chosen by a combination of an online public vote and a panel of experts.

Ramsdale's vital save to deny Bournemouth's Dango Ouattara won March's Premier League Save of the Month award. It prevented Arsenal from going 2–0 down after 21 minutes of a match they ultimately went on to win 3–2 with Reiss Nelson netting the last-gasp winner.<ref name="Ramsdale claimed March's PL SOTM"/> His flying fingertip save to stop Liverpool's Salah from scoring a deflected curling shot in stoppage time won April's award. It secured the Gunners a 2–2 draw at Anfield.<ref name="Ramsdale claimed April's PL SOTM"/>

===Debuts or 100th appearances===
As a schoolboy midfielder at the age of 15 years and 181 days, Nwaneri became the [[Premier League records and statistics#Player records|youngest player]] in Premier League history when he came on as a substitute against Brentford in September.<ref name="BRE v ARS PL BBC"/> He also became [[List of Arsenal F.C. records and statistics#Player records|Arsenal's youngest-ever player]] in any senior competition.<ref name="season statistics AFC"/>
